meanings.def: (before a verb, as in 一...就...) as soon as; once

compositionNote: The simplest possible mark — one unbroken line — pictographically stands for the number one itself.
poem: One flat line upon the ground,
the very first count ever found.
No bend, no curve, just plain and true,
ONE (yī) is the stroke where numbers grew.

compositionNote: Simply two parallel lines stacked one above the other, doubling the single stroke of 一 to picture 'two'.
poem: Two flat lines, stacked up neat,
doubling one to make a pair complete.
Sky on top, the ground below,
TWO (èr) is how the counting starts to grow.

compositionNote: One more line stacked on 二 gives three parallel strokes, simply counting one higher.
poem: Add one more line atop the two,
now three flat strokes come into view.
Heaven, man, and earth in a row,
THREE (sān) is the trio, steady and slow.

compositionNote: A pair of legs (儿) fenced inside a boundary (囗) replaced the four tally-lines of oracle-bone script to write the number four.
poem: Legs tucked inside a fenced-in square,
a boxed-in strider, penned in there.
Four tally lines once stood in a row,
FOUR (sì) is the count this fence will show.

components.meaning: an X shape crossing between two bars, symbolizing interacting forces

compositionNote: An ancient X-shape crossing between two horizontal lines pictured heaven and earth's forces meeting, later fixed as the numeral five.
poem: Two flat bars with an X locked tight,
crossing forces of dark and light.
Where heaven and earth cross and bend,
FIVE (wǔ) is the count where they extend.

compositionNote: A small roof (亠) over two splitting legs (八) once pictured a simple hut; the shape was later borrowed purely for its sound to write six.
poem: A tiny roof with legs that splay,
a little hut from far away.
Borrowed now for sound alone,
SIX (liù) is the number that hut has grown.

components.meaning: a line crossed by a hooked cutting stroke

compositionNote: A horizontal line crossed by a hooked stroke once pictured cutting something in two; the shape was later borrowed to write the number seven.
poem: A line sliced through by a hooking blade,
an ancient cut that time has made.
Borrowed sound, forgetting the knife,
SEVEN (qī) counts through daily life.

components.meaning: two strokes curving apart, from a picture of something splitting in two

compositionNote: Two small strokes leaning away from each other originally pictured something being split apart; the shape was borrowed to write the number eight.
poem: Two little strokes that lean and part,
splitting cleanly right from the start.
Back to back, they gently sway,
EIGHT (bā) is the number that split away.

components.meaning: a bent, hooked arm, from an ancient pictograph

compositionNote: A single curling stroke once pictured a bent elbow or hooked arm; borrowed for its sound, it became the numeral nine.
poem: A curling hook, an elbow bent,
an ancient arm's own shape it lent.
Twist and turn, then curve some more,
NINE (jiǔ) sits one shy of a perfect score.

components.meaning: a vertical line crossed by a horizontal one, from a knot tied in a tally cord

compositionNote: A simple cross shape once marked a knot tied in a counting cord for every ten items, giving the character its meaning of ten.
poem: A cross of lines, both straight and true,
a knot once tied when counts hit ten.
Vertical meets horizontal too,
TEN (shí) is the round count born again.

meanings.def: fragmentary; odd; leftover (as in extra small amounts)

compositionNote: Rain (雨) falling as scattered drops gave the original sense of 'fragment, remainder', while 令 lends the sound líng; the word later came to mean 'zero', the emptiest fragment of all.
poem: Raindrops scatter, fragment, fall,
tiny remnants, that is all.
An order (令) gives the sound so clear,
ZERO (líng) is the emptiest drop of the year.

compositionNote: One (一) capping 白, which lends its sound (bái becoming bǎi), builds the numeral for a full hundred.
poem: One small stroke sits on top of white,
a hundred units, gleaming bright.
White (白) lends its sound, plain to hear,
A HUNDRED (bǎi) counted, loud and clear.

meanings.def: generic measure word for people or objects

components.meaning: a single stalk of bamboo, from an ancient pictograph

compositionNote: The character began as a picture of one stalk of bamboo standing among many in a grove, making it a natural generic counter for individual things.
poem: One lone bamboo stalk stands tall,
a single stem among them all.
Count the stalks one by one, you see,
EACH (gè) item gets its own bamboo key.

components.meaning: a person walking, seen from the side

compositionNote: A simple pictograph of two legs in mid-stride, viewed from the side, drawing a person in motion.
poem: Two legs striding, side in view,
one leg forward, walking through.
A simple sketch of you and me,
PERSON (rén) is all humanity.

components.meaning: an ancient serrated halberd or weapon

compositionNote: The character originally drew a jagged, saw-toothed weapon; because its sound matched, it was borrowed to write the first-person pronoun 'I', losing its weapon meaning entirely.
poem: A jagged blade with saw-tooth bite,
an ancient weapon, sharp in sight.
Its shape stuck, but not its blow,
'I' (wǒ) is all it means, you know.

compositionNote: A person (亻) stands beside 尔, an old word for 'you' that also lends its sound, pointing straight at the person you're speaking to.
poem: A person standing right by 尔,
the ancient word that once meant 'you'.
Point a finger, greet them well,
YOU (nǐ) is the one I'm talking to.

compositionNote: A person (亻) next to 也, which supplies the sound tā, forms the third-person pronoun 'he'.
poem: A person leans on 也 too,
also here, as people do.
Not you, not me, but someone new,
HE (tā) is the other person in view.

compositionNote: A woman (女) paired with the sound-giving 也 (tā) created the modern feminine pronoun 'she', coined in the early 1900s to mirror 他.
poem: A woman stands by 也 as well,
also here, the same to tell.
Swap the person for the girl,
SHE (tā) steps into the word-whirl.

compositionNote: The character began as a picture of a coiled snake tucked beneath a roof-like curve; it later lost that literal meaning and was borrowed as the pronoun 'it'.
poem: A snake once curled beneath its roof,
tail tucked in, safe and aloof.
No longer slithering, just a name,
IT (tā) is what non-humans became.

meanings.def: plural marker attached after pronouns or people

compositionNote: A person (亻) beside a door (门), which lends its sound men, marks that more than one person is passing through — the plural suffix.
poem: One by one through the door they come,
person after person, not just one.
The gate (门) lets many pass again,
PLURAL is marked by this little men (men).

components.meaning: a bird flying upward, disappearing from sight

compositionNote: The character originally pictured a bird flying up until it vanished from view — the idea of something no longer being there gave rise to the negative 'not'.
poem: A bird flies up and out of sight,
vanishing into fading light.
Gone from view, it won't come back,
NOT (bù) is what that bird will lack.

compositionNote: The sun (日) sits above a mark for 'straight, correct' (正, shown in a slightly altered form), the idea being that what the sun reveals is true — hence 'to be; is'.
poem: The sun shines straight and never lies,
correct and true beneath the skies.
What the sun sees, it will affirm,
'TO BE' (shì) is the sun's own certain term.

meanings.def: possessive/attributive particle linking a modifier to a noun ('s, of)

compositionNote: The character originally pictured something bright and clear (白) marked by a small ladle-shaped stroke (勺), meaning a clear 'target'; this common word was later borrowed as the everyday possessive particle 'de'.
poem: Bright white target, clear and small,
a tiny ladle scoops it all.
Just a little linking key,
POSSESSIVE de ties things, you see.

meanings.def: marks a completed action after a verb
marks a change of state at the end of a sentence

components.meaning: a bent hook, from an ancient picture of a swaddled child

compositionNote: The character once pictured a swaddled child with arms wrapped close to the body; the sense of being 'bound up, finished' led to its use as the marker of completed action.
poem: A tiny hook, all bent and small,
a swaddled babe, arms wrapped and all.
Wrapped up snug, the deed is done,
COMPLETE is le — the action's won.

meanings.def: to be located at; to exist
(before a verb) in the process of

compositionNote: Standing firmly on the earth (土), with 才 lending its sound zài, the character expresses being located somewhere.
poem: Feet planted firm upon the earth (土),
rooted right where you find your worth.
Talent (才) whispers its sound today,
LOCATED here is where you stay (zài).

compositionNote: A hand (又, shown as the slanted stroke on top) reaching down to grasp a piece of meat (月, originally 肉) pictures the basic act of possessing something.
poem: A hand reaches down, grabs some meat,
holding tight to something to eat.
Grip it firm, don't let it go,
TO HAVE (yǒu) is the oldest 'possess', you know.

compositionNote: Movement (辶) paired with a sound-component (文, simplified from the original phonetic 言) points to something close at hand as you move toward it — 'this'.
poem: Walking (辶) toward the words (文) you see,
step by step, right up close to me.
Point right here, no need to guess,
THIS (zhè) is the one within your reach.

compositionNote: A phonetic element from an ancient place name (冄) stands beside the 'city' radical (阝, from 邑), since 那 first named a distant region before it came to mean 'that'.
poem: A far-off town (阝) with a name of old,
a place (冄) whose story has been told.
Point across the distant plain,
THAT (nà) is the far one, not so plain.

compositionNote: A mouth (口) asking a question sits beside 那 (nà), which supplies the sound, turning 'that' into the question word 'which'.
poem: A mouth (口) pops open, asking 'that'? (那)
Which one, though? Point me where it's at!
A curious voice with a questioning air,
WHICH (nǎ) one is it — tell me where.

compositionNote: Spoken words (讠) beside a little bird (隹, lending its sound zhuī toward shéi) form the question word asking about an unnamed person — 'who'.
poem: Words (讠) fly out to ask about a face,
a little bird (隹) sings from its place.
A mystery voice calls through the air,
WHO (shéi) is singing? Tell me who's there.

compositionNote: A person (亻) next to the numeral ten (十) originally named a squad of ten soldiers; today the character survives mainly in the question word 什么, 'what'.
poem: Ten (十) soldiers standing in a line,
one person (亻) counted every time.
Now the meaning's shifted, though —
WHAT (shén) could this old squad still show?

meanings.def: toneless suffix with no meaning of its own, used in 什么, 这么, 那么, 怎么

components.meaning: a thin twisted thread, from a picture of fine silk (a variant of 幺)

compositionNote: The character pictures a small twisted strand of silk — something tiny and slight — and today survives only as a light, toneless suffix in words like 什么 and 怎么.
poem: A tiny thread, so thin and light,
twisted silk, barely in sight.
No weight of meaning does it hold,
just a soft SUFFIX (me), story untold.

meanings.def: turns a statement into a yes/no question

compositionNote: A mouth (口) asking something sits beside 马 (mǎ), which lends its sound, forming the simple question particle 'ma' placed at the end of a sentence.
poem: A mouth (口) pops open to ask, you see,
a horse (马) gallops by, wild and free.
Tack it on the end of what you say,
QUESTION particle ma — yes or nay?

meanings.def: softens a question or asks 'and...what about...?'

compositionNote: A mouth (口) speaking sits beside 尼 (ní), which lends its sound, forming the soft question particle 'ne' used to ask 'and what about...?'.
poem: A mouth (口) leans in, soft words it lends,
a gentle nun (尼) whose calm tone bends.
'And what about...?' the question flows free,
that lingering NE (ne) finishes gently.

compositionNote: Grain (禾, also lending its sound hé) feeding a mouth (口) pictures shared food and contentment, giving the sense of 'harmony', which extended to the everyday connector 'and'.
poem: Grain (禾) shared out to feed each mouth (口),
peace grows in from north to south.
Link one thing with another, see —
AND (hé) joins us all in harmony.

compositionNote: Walking (彳) alongside 艮, a stubborn, unyielding element that lends its sound gěn toward hěn, intensified over time into the everyday adverb 'very'.
poem: Steps (彳) march on, stubborn and set,
hard as stone (艮), no doubt or fret.
Push it further, to the max degree —
VERY (hěn) means 'to the utmost', you see.

compositionNote: A woman (女) beside her child (子) — the ancient picture of all being good and well.
poem: A mother and her child,
together, reconciled —
when woman meets with son,
then GOOD (hǎo) has begun!

components.meaning: a person standing with arms and legs spread wide

compositionNote: An ancient picture of a person standing with arms flung wide, taking up as much space as possible — the very picture of 'big'.
poem: Arms flung wide, legs spread apart,
a stick-figure giant from the start.
Take up space, stand tall and proud —
BIG (dà) and mighty, big and loud!

components.meaning: three tiny dots, like grains of sand or specks of dust

compositionNote: A pictograph of tiny specks so small they could be swept up with one hand — hence 'small'.
poem: Three tiny grains, so small they fall,
swept aside, not big at all.
Pinch them close with finger and thumb —
SMALL (xiǎo) is what these three specks become.

components.meaning: evening (originally a piece of meat, 肉)
evening (originally a piece of meat, 肉)

compositionNote: Two pieces of meat (夕, originally 肉) stacked one on top of the other, showing a growing pile — hence 'many'.
poem: Two chunks of meat piled on a plate,
stacked up high, they simply can't wait.
Pile on more, don't hold it back —
MANY (duō) means plenty, stack on stack!

components.meaning: a stroke cutting away, showing something removed

compositionNote: One more small stroke is sliced away from 小 (small), leaving even less behind — so 少 means 'few'.
poem: Small (小) got a stroke sliced clean away,
less and less with each passing day.
What was little shrinks once more —
FEW (shǎo) is smaller than before.

meanings.def: to go up; to get on; to attend

components.meaning: a short mark placed above a horizontal baseline

compositionNote: An indicative symbol: a short stroke sits above a baseline (一), pointing straight at the idea of 'above'.
poem: A dash floats high above the ground,
pointing up without a sound.
Climb the ladder, rise, don't stall —
UP (shàng) and over, above it all.

meanings.def: to go down; to get off

components.meaning: a short mark placed below a horizontal baseline

compositionNote: An indicative symbol: a short stroke sits below a baseline (一), pointing straight at the idea of 'below'.
poem: A dash sinks low beneath the line,
dropping down, that's its design.
Gravity pulls, so let it fall —
DOWN (xià) and under, below it all.

components.meaning: a footprint, meaning to walk or advance (worn down to 䒑 at the top)
originally a boat (舟), now shaped like the moon radical

compositionNote: Originally a foot (止) stepping onto a boat (舟, now written 月) with a knife (刀) cutting the mooring line — the picture of moving onward, hence 'front, before'.
poem: A foot steps down onto a boat,
knife cuts the rope, and off they float.
Sailing onward, leading the way —
FRONT (qián) is ahead, come what may.

components.meaning: a person, turned to represent a ruler

compositionNote: A ruler (人) gives orders with the mouth (口) — originally 'sovereign; queen', later borrowed as the simplified form meaning 'behind, after'.
poem: A ruler turns, his mouth commands,
issuing orders through the land.
But turn around, and there you'll see —
BEHIND (hòu) is where the queen will be.

compositionNote: A field (田) of earth (土) — originally a village where people farmed and lived, later coming to mean 'inside' and a measure of distance.
poem: A field of earth, soil dark and deep,
inside the village, safe to keep.
Step through the gate, come stay a while —
INSIDE (lǐ) this place, walk every mile.

components.meaning: to divine (a crack pattern on an oracle bone)

compositionNote: Divining (卜) in the evening (夕), an unusual time to do it, was 'outside' normal custom — hence 外 means 'outside'.
poem: At dusk, a diviner cracks the bone,
reading signs from the great unknown.
Odd hour, place beyond the door —
OUTSIDE (wài) is what it stands for.

components.meaning: a vertical line piercing straight through

compositionNote: A line (丨) runs straight through the center of a shape (口), like an arrow hitting dead center on a target — hence 'middle'.
poem: An arrow flies and finds its mark,
straight through the center, hits the bark.
Not left, not right, but dead-on true —
MIDDLE (zhōng) is the aim that flew.

meanings.def: host; owner (in compounds like 房东, 股东)

components.meaning: tree (visible in the traditional form 東)
sun (visible in the traditional form 東)

compositionNote: The traditional form 東 showed the sun (日) rising up behind a tree (木) — the direction the sun comes from: east. The simplified 东 keeps only a trace of that picture.
poem: The sun climbs up behind a tree,
glowing bright for all to see.
Where morning light first starts to spring —
EAST (dōng) is that bright rising thing.

components.meaning: a bird settling into its nest at sunset

compositionNote: An ancient picture of a bird settling into its nest as the sun goes down — the direction of sunset is 'west'.
poem: A little bird flies home at last,
settling in as daylight's passed.
Where the sun dips low and mild —
WEST (xī) is dusk's returning child.

components.meaning: an ancient hanging bell-shaped instrument, faced south in ritual

compositionNote: An ancient picture of a hanging musical instrument, traditionally set facing the warm southern direction during rituals — giving 南 its meaning of 'south'.
poem: A hanging bell, ancient and grand,
faced the warmth of sunlit land.
Toward the heat, the bright, the wide —
SOUTH (nán) is that sunny side.

compositionNote: Two people stand back to back, facing away from each other — since houses traditionally faced south, the sunless, back-facing direction became 'north'.
poem: Two people stand back to back,
turned away from the sunny track.
Cold and shaded, dim the light —
NORTH (běi) is the chilly side of night.

components.meaning: one; a line representing what lies above
a person standing with arms outstretched

compositionNote: A line (一) drawn above a person (大) shows what is above a person's head — the sky, and by extension 'heaven' and 'day'.
poem: A line floats high above a man,
stretching over all the land.
Above his head, the blue does reign —
SKY (tiān) each day, and bright again.

components.meaning: grain; a ripe crop (seen in the original form)
person, carrying the harvest (seen in the original form)

compositionNote: Originally a picture of a person (人) carrying a bundle of ripe grain (禾) on their back — one harvest cycle marked a 'year'.
poem: A farmer bends beneath the load,
grain piled high along the road.
One harvest done, the seasons spin —
YEAR (nián) is a cycle wrapping in.

components.meaning: a crescent moon, seen hanging in the sky

compositionNote: A picture of a crescent moon — the character for 'moon', and since the moon's cycle marks roughly thirty days, also 'month'.
poem: A silver sliver curves up high,
a crescent hanging in the sky.
Each cycle marks a month within —
the MOON (yuè) is where new months begin.

components.meaning: a round sun with a mark at its center

compositionNote: A picture of the round sun with a dot at its heart — the character for 'sun', and since one sunrise marks one day, also 'day'.
poem: A circle glows with a dot at heart,
a burning sun, a fiery art.
It rises once to start the day —
SUN (rì) and day, both come this way.

components.meaning: a bright celestial body, like the sun
to grow; be born — used here for its sound (phonetic)

compositionNote: A bright object in the sky (日) combines with 生 (shēng), used here for its sound, to write 'star'.
poem: The sun (日) gave birth (生) to sparks of light,
scattered specks across the night.
Tiny, bright, and far away —
STARS (xīng) that twinkle till the day.

components.meaning: that; his/her/its — used here for its sound (phonetic)
moon, representing the passage of time

compositionNote: The moon (月) marks the passing of time, while 其 (qí) lends its sound — together forming 期, 'a period of time'.
poem: The moon (月) keeps count as it shows its face,
其 lends the sound that gives it grace.
Days and weeks in cycles spin —
a TERM (qī), a period locked within.

components.meaning: a lid or cover, coming together

compositionNote: A lid (亼) closes down over something and holds it close — the present moment, right now, hence 今 means 'now'.
poem: A lid comes down and seals it tight,
holding this moment, day or night.
Not past, not future, only here —
NOW (jīn) is the moment, always near.

compositionNote: The sun (日) by day and the moon (月) by night, the two brightest lights in the sky, combine to mean 'bright'.
poem: The sun (日) by day, the moon (月) by night,
together they make double bright.
Two lamps combined can never dim —
BRIGHT (míng) is the glow that comes from them.

components.meaning: suddenly; just now — used here for its sound (phonetic)

compositionNote: The day (日) that has just passed — with 乍 lending its sound — gives 昨, 'yesterday'.
poem: The sun (日) that shone has since moved on,
sudden (乍) as the day is gone.
Look behind you, not so near —
YESTERDAY (zuó) is always here.

components.meaning: jade (玉), whose polished shine becomes visible

compositionNote: Jade (王, from 玉) becomes visible to the eye (见) once polished — showing what appears right now, hence 现 means 'present; to appear'.
poem: Jade (玉) shines bright before the eye (见),
its hidden gleam no longer shy.
Right before us, plain to see —
NOW (xiàn) it shows, for you and me.

components.meaning: sun, marking the passage of time
temple — used here for its sound (phonetic)

compositionNote: The sun (日) tracks the passing hours, while 寺 lends its sound — together forming 时, 'time'.
poem: The sun (日) ticks by, a temple's (寺) bell,
counting hours it knows so well.
Hour by hour, the moments climb —
TIME (shí) is the sound of passing time.

components.meaning: marquis; nobleman — used here mainly for its sound (phonetic), with an extra stroke added

compositionNote: A person (亻) stands watching and waiting, with 侯 lending its sound — giving 候, 'to wait' and 'a period of time'.
poem: A person (亻) waits, a marquis's (侯) name,
watching, patient, just the same.
Standing still as moments pass —
WAIT (hòu), the time will come at last.

meanings.def: minute; a small fractional unit (money, score)

components.meaning: eight; here a picture of two strokes splitting apart

compositionNote: A knife (刀) cuts something into two separate parts (八) — hence 分 means 'to divide', and by extension a small divided unit like a 'minute'.
poem: A knife (刀) comes down and cuts things two (八),
splitting parts from something new.
Break it down, share and spend —
DIVIDE (fēn), and minutes bend.

components.meaning: middle — used here for its sound (phonetic)

compositionNote: A metal (钅) object with 中 lending its sound — giving 钟, a metal bell or clock.
poem: A metal (钅) bell rings dead center (中),
tolling hours as they enter.
Tick and chime, the sound rings true —
CLOCK (zhōng) is what it says to you.

components.meaning: to occupy — used here for its sound (phonetic)
fire, shown as four small flickering dots

compositionNote: A flickering flame (灬) with 占 lending its sound — together giving 点, a tiny bright 'dot', and by extension a 'point' in time.
poem: A flame (灬) flickers, small and bright,
占 lends its sound to catch the light.
Tiny spark upon the wall —
a DOT (diǎn), a point, an hour's call.

compositionNote: An ox (牛) split (八) right down the middle — since oxen are large and easily divided, 半 came to mean 'half'.

words.meaning: half a day; a long while

poem: An ox (牛) is split (八) right down the seam,
divided evenly, it would seem.
Not whole, not none, just in between —
HALF (bàn) is the fairest share I've seen.

components.meaning: mountain-like shape, worn down from an original footstep 止
evening, echoing the passing of time

compositionNote: The traditional 歲 combined two footsteps marking the passage of time with an axe for its sound; the simplified 岁 keeps a mountain-like top (山) and 夕, still tracking each year that passes.
poem: A mountain step, an evening glow,
marking years as seasons go.
Each birthday climbed, a peak to gain —
YEARS OLD (suì) counted, again, again.

components.meaning: a bent shape representing breath escaping — a cry or call

compositionNote: A mouth (口) lets out a cry (丂) — originally 'to call out', later used for a numbered mark, like the 'number' of a date.
poem: A mouth (口) lets out a bending cry (丂),
calling loud beneath the sky.
Give it digits, give it place —
NUMBER (hào) marks the date, the space.

meanings.def: to be called (name); to call out; to shout

components.meaning: twisted cords — used here for its sound (phonetic)

compositionNote: A mouth (口) calls out loudly, with 丩 lending its sound — giving 叫, 'to call' or 'to shout'.

words.meaning: to be called; to be known as

poem: A mouth (口) shouts out, twisted (丩) and loud,
calling names out of the crowd.
Raise your voice, don't be shy —
CALL (jiào) it out, give it a try.

compositionNote: At dusk (夕), when faces could no longer be seen, people called out with their mouths (口) to identify themselves — hence 名 means 'name'.
poem: At dusk (夕), no face is left to see,
so mouths (口) call out, "It's me, it's me!"
Spoken loud so all may know —
NAME (míng) is the word we call and show.

compositionNote: A child (子) is sheltered under a roof (宀), just as a written character shelters and carries meaning.
poem: Under a roof, snug and small,
a child learns to write it all.
Stroke by stroke, a mark, a sign —
that's a CHARACTER (zì), yours and mine.

compositionNote: A precious jade (玉) guarded within an enclosure (囗) pictures the treasured land of a country.
poem: Inside four walls, a jewel of jade,
guarded well, its worth displayed.
Borders drawn, a realm construed —
that's a COUNTRY (guó), whole and true.

meanings.def: the Han people; Chinese (as in 汉语, 汉字)

components.meaning: hand; again — used here as a sound hint

compositionNote: The water radical (氵), from the Han River, combines with 又 as a sound hint to give hàn — the Han people and their language.
poem: By the river, hands at play,
Han folk lived along its way.
Their name in flowing water again —
say HAN (hàn), the people of the plain.

components.meaning: I; me — used here as a sound hint

compositionNote: Speech (讠) plus 吾 (‘I/me’, a sound hint) forms yǔ — the words that come out when a person speaks: language.
poem: Words pour out when 'I' would speak,
sentences form, week by week.
Sound and tongue, in speech imbued —
that's LANGUAGE (yǔ), spoken and construed.

components.meaning: a pictograph of crossed decorative lines, like a pattern tattooed on a chest

compositionNote: 文 pictures crossed ornamental lines — the ancient image of pattern and marking that grew into ‘writing’ and ‘culture’.
poem: Crossed lines etched on ancient skin,
patterns marking where art begins.
From old tattoos, this sign was spun —
that's WRITING (wén), and culture as one.

compositionNote: Crossed strokes on top (representing guiding hands) sit above a cover (冖) and a child (子) — hands guiding a child under a roof to learn.
poem: Hands up above reach down with care,
guiding a child 'neath the roof up there.
Lesson by lesson, day by day —
that's how we LEARN (xué) and find our way.

meanings.def: to be born; to give birth to

components.meaning: a pictograph of a tender shoot pushing up out of the ground

compositionNote: 生 pictures a young shoot breaking through the soil — the image of birth, growth, and life.
poem: A tender shoot breaks through the ground,
pushing up without a sound.
New and green, it starts to grow —
that's LIFE (shēng) beginning, don't you know.

meanings.def: prefix showing familiarity or respect, e.g. 老师, 老朋友

components.meaning: long hair of an elderly person (a variant of 老)
a bent figure, like a person leaning on a cane

compositionNote: 老 pictures an elderly person with long hair (耂) bent over like a cane (匕) — the image of old age.
poem: Long white hair, a bended cane,
walking slow through wind and rain.
Wisdom carried, year by year —
that's OLD (lǎo) age, drawing near.

meanings.def: specialist; expert (in compounds like 医师)

components.meaning: an ancient sign for a mound of earth; troops stationed there

compositionNote: A flag (巾) planted beside a troop mound (𠂤) once marked an army's leader; the meaning shifted to a skilled leader — a teacher or master.
poem: A banner raised above the crowd,
leading troops, calling loud.
Now it guides young minds instead —
that's the TEACHER (shī), out ahead.

compositionNote: Under one covering frame (冂), everyone shares a single mouth or voice (口) — the picture of being together, the same.
poem: One roof covers everyone,
one mouth speaking, joined as one.
No two voices, just one tone —
that means SAME (tóng), never alone.

components.meaning: to cross; to exchange — used here as a sound hint

compositionNote: Wood (木, once wooden shackles for training) pairs with 交 as a sound hint to give xiào — the place where students are trained: school.
poem: Wood once bound a lesson tight,
crossed with rules to make it right.
Now it's where the students go —
that's the SCHOOL (xiào) where knowledge grows.

compositionNote: A pig (豕) kept under a roof (宀) pictures the ancient farming household — home and family.
poem: Under a roof, warm and dry,
a pig is kept, the years go by.
Where the hearth and heart are found —
that's your HOME (jiā), your family's ground.

components.meaning: used here purely as a sound hint

compositionNote: Father (父) pairs with 巴 purely as a sound hint to spell bà — dad.
poem: Father's hand held firm and true,
巴 just lends the sound to you.
Call him loud, call him near —
that's DAD (bà), forever here.

components.meaning: horse — used here as a sound hint

compositionNote: Woman (女) plus 马 as a sound hint gives mā — mom.
poem: A woman riding on a horse,
galloping home, of course, of course.
Fast and warm, she comes to greet —
that's MOM (mā), so kind and sweet.

meanings.def: retroflex suffix -r attached to nouns (erhua), e.g. 花儿

components.meaning: a pictograph of a pair of legs, representing a person or child

compositionNote: 儿 pictures a pair of little legs — the simplified image of a young child.
poem: Just two little legs on the run,
scampering off before they're done.
Small and quick, this little one —
that's a CHILD (ér), full of fun.

components.meaning: a pictograph of a woman kneeling gracefully with arms folded

compositionNote: 女 pictures a woman kneeling gracefully with arms crossed — the ancient image of a woman.
poem: Kneeling gently, arms held low,
grace and calm in every bow.
An ancient picture, soft and clear —
that's WOMAN (nǚ), drawn right here.

meanings.def: noun suffix attached to many nouns, e.g. 桌子, 孩子

components.meaning: a pictograph of a swaddled baby with arms outstretched

compositionNote: 子 pictures a baby wrapped in a blanket with arms reaching out — the image of a child.
poem: Wrapped up snug in a blanket tight,
tiny arms reach for the light.
Bundled small, held with love —
that's a CHILD (zǐ), sent from above.

meanings.def: friend (bound form, used mainly in 朋友)

components.meaning: originally a string of paired cowrie shells, not the moon
a matching second string of shells

compositionNote: 朋 originally pictured two strings of cowrie shells tied together — things paired side by side, later meaning companions.
poem: Two strings of shells, side by side,
tied together, matched with pride.
Paired as one, wherever we roam —
that's a FRIEND (péng), your second home.

compositionNote: Two hands (又 and 又) reaching out and clasping together picture friendship — being of one mind with someone.
poem: One hand reaches, then another,
clasped together like a brother.
Side by side, we walk life's road —
that's a FRIEND (yǒu), sharing the load.

components.meaning: a modified form of 之/止, meaning a foot stepping forward

compositionNote: A foot stepping out (top strokes) ahead of a person's legs (儿) shows someone moving out in front — first, before.
poem: A foot steps out ahead of the rest,
past the legs, it leads the quest.
Out in front, before the crowd —
that means FIRST (xiān), stepping proud.

compositionNote: An arrow (矢, once used to probe wounds) kept in a case (匚) pictures the tools of healing — medicine.
poem: An arrow kept inside a case,
once used to heal, to probe, to trace.
Tools for tending every ill —
that's MEDICINE (yī), and healing skill.

components.meaning: complete — used here as a sound hint

compositionNote: A walled enclosure (阝) pairs with 完 as a sound hint to give yuàn — a courtyard, and by extension an institution like a hospital.
poem: A wall stands round, complete and whole,
enclosing a yard, a healing goal.
Step inside its gated door —
that's the COURTYARD (yuàn), and so much more.

compositionNote: 商 pictures a trader standing (立) on a tall stall, calling out (口) to advertise his wares — commerce, business.
poem: Standing tall upon his stand,
calling loud across the land.
Selling wares from dawn to night —
that's COMMERCE (shāng), a merchant's sight.

components.meaning: to occupy; to claim a spot

compositionNote: A building (广) where someone has staked out a spot (占) to sell goods — a shop.
poem: A building where a spot's been claimed,
goods on shelves, all neatly named.
Open the door and step on in —
that's the SHOP (diàn) where sales begin.

components.meaning: evolved from a net (网) cast over shells/money (贝) — reaching out to acquire goods

compositionNote: 买's shape comes from a net (网) held over money or shells (贝) — the ancient image of gathering goods to buy.
poem: A net cast wide, a coin below,
reaching out for what you owe.
Hand it over, take it home —
that's to BUY (mǎi), no need to roam.

components.meaning: a worn-down form of 出 (‘to go out’)

compositionNote: 卖 stacks 十 (a simplified form of 出, ‘to go out’) on top of 买 (‘to buy’) — sending goods out to be bought: to sell.
poem: Stack 十 on top of buying's frame,
sending goods out, just the same.
Out the door, into the crowd —
that's to SELL (mài), announced out loud.

components.meaning: metal — early coins were cast in bronze
small; piled up — used here as a sound and meaning hint

compositionNote: Metal (钅), since coins were cast in bronze, combines with 戋 (small bits piled up) as a sound hint to give qián — money.
poem: Metal melted, coins piled small,
counted careful, one and all.
Jingling pockets, spend with care —
that's the MONEY (qián) that we share.

components.meaning: to break off; decisive — used here as a sound hint

compositionNote: A clump of earth (土) broken off (夬) pictures a piece or chunk — and casually, a dollar.
poem: A clump of earth, broken free,
counted out for you and me.
One small chunk, or coins you keep —
that's a PIECE (kuài), never cheap.

components.meaning: a pictograph of a tall multi-story tower — roof on top, window in the middle, doorway below

compositionNote: 高 pictures a tall tower: a roof on top, a window in the middle, and a doorway (口) at the base — giving the meaning ‘tall, high’.
poem: A tower stands with roof on top,
windows, doorway, doesn't stop.
Reaching upward, proud and bold —
that's so HIGH (gāo), a sight to behold.

meanings.def: happy; in high spirits (as in 高兴)

components.meaning: simplified from 興, a picture of four hands raising an object together

compositionNote: 兴 comes from 興, a picture of four hands lifting something up together — the shared lift of excitement and interest.
poem: Four hands lift something up in glee,
raising joy for all to see.
Shared delight, a common cheer —
that's feeling EXCITED (xìng), joy sincere.

meanings.def: to like; to be fond of

components.meaning: a drum set on a stand

compositionNote: 喜 pictures a drum (壴) being beaten while a joyful mouth (口) sings along — the image of joy and happiness.
poem: A drum beats loud, a joyful sound,
mouths sing along, all around.
Celebration fills the air —
that's pure HAPPINESS (xǐ), everywhere.

components.meaning: hand — a remnant of the original phonetic 雚
a person with mouth wide open, as if yawning or exhaling

compositionNote: A hand (又, a remnant of the original phonetic 雚) beside a person with mouth wide open (欠) pictures joyful shouting — to be happy.
poem: A mouth flung open, shouting cheer,
hands clapping loud, drawing near.
Laughter rises, joy on tap —
that's being HAPPY (huān), joy's own lap.

meanings.def: to love; to be fond of

components.meaning: a hand reaching down, like a claw

compositionNote: A hand reaches down (爫) and shelters (冖) a friend (友) — simplified 爱 famously left out the heart (心) from the middle, yet still means love.
poem: A hand reaches down, a cover spread,
holding a friend close instead.
No heart drawn in, yet still it's true —
that's called LOVE (ài), given to you.

meanings.def: to visit; to see (a doctor, a friend)

components.meaning: hand, drawn here without its hook

compositionNote: A hand (手) shading the eyes (目) pictures someone peering into the distance — to look, to see.
poem: A hand shades the eye from the sun,
peering far till the searching's done.
Watching close, near and far —
that's to LOOK (kàn) at where things are.

meanings.def: to see; to catch sight of

compositionNote: An eye (目) sitting on top of a pair of legs (儿) pictures a person looking out — to see, to meet.
poem: An eye sits high on walking legs,
scanning round, no room for dregs.
Spotting friends out on the street —
that's to SEE (jiàn), and then to meet.

components.meaning: axe — used here as a sound hint

compositionNote: A mouth (口) paired with 斤 as a sound hint gives tīng — to listen, to hear.
poem: A mouth leans in, an axe rings clear,
sound waves travel to the ear.
Quiet now, and lend an ear —
that's to LISTEN (tīng), far and near.

meanings.def: to speak; to say; to explain

components.meaning: to exchange; also a sound hint

compositionNote: The speech radical 讠 shows the meaning ('words'), while 兑 lends its sound to give shuō.
poem: Words (讠) get traded like a deal (兑),
mouths swap sounds that thoughts reveal.
Open up and let it flow —
that's shuō, the words you know.

meanings.def: to read; to study, to attend school

components.meaning: to sell; a sound hint for dú

compositionNote: Speech 讠 shows this is about words, while 卖 (sell) supplies a sound clue for dú.
poem: Words (讠) for sale (卖), lined on a shelf,
you buy each page and read it yourself.
Eyes move on, page by page —
dú means READ, at any age.

components.meaning: a cover, from the roof 宀 in the old form
visual remnant replacing 舄 (a bird) in the old form

compositionNote: Originally 寫 showed a magpie (舄) under a roof (宀), borrowed for 'to write'; the simplified 写 keeps a cover (冖) over a reduced stroke shape resembling 与.
poem: Under a cozy cover (冖) small,
a bird once perched, hard to recall.
Now hand meets paper, ink takes flight —
xiě (写) means simply: to WRITE.

meanings.def: can, to be able to (a learned skill)

components.meaning: cloud-like shape below, a simplified stand-in for the complex traditional form

compositionNote: A person (人) sits above a cloud-like shape (云) — a simplified graphic form standing in for the more complex traditional 會, now meaning 'can' or 'meeting'.
poem: A person (人) floats on a cloud (云) so high,
learning tricks as they drift by.
Master a skill, then you CAN too —
huì's the word for all you do.

components.meaning: a curled shape, part of an old bear's head
a paw shape (appears twice, as legs)

compositionNote: 能 originally drew a bear — head (厶), body (月), and two paws (匕匕) — a creature admired for its strength and ABILITY.
poem: A bear's body (月) and two strong paws (匕匕),
strong enough to break the laws.
That mighty strength means you CAN do it —
néng's the power flowing through it.

meanings.def: would like to, to want to

compositionNote: The heart (心) sits beneath 相 (xiāng), which lends its sound and a sense of looking at one another — thinking of someone with your heart.
poem: Two eyes look mutual (相), face to face,
then rest upon a heart's warm place (心).
That's how you THINK, or miss someone —
xiǎng, the wish beneath the sun.

components.meaning: west; here a worn-down shape from the original picture of a waist

compositionNote: 要 originally pictured a woman (女) with her hands on her waist (the top shape, now resembling 西) — later borrowed to mean 'to want' or 'important'.
poem: Hands on her hips (西), a woman (女) stands,
deciding firmly what she demands.
"I WANT this now!" — that's her decree,
yào's the wish, plain to see.

compositionNote: Speech 讠 shows this is about polite words, while 青 supplies the sound qīng, softened to qǐng.
poem: Fresh green words (青) spoken (讠) soft and light,
"PLEASE, come join us here tonight."
Polite requests in a gentle tone,
qǐng's the manner, kindly known.

compositionNote: Words (讠) come from the body (身) and hand (寸) together — a bow and spoken gratitude combined to say THANKS.
poem: Words (讠) leave the body (身), hand (寸) held near,
a bow, a phrase, sincere and clear.
"THANK you so much," is what we've meant,
xiè's the grateful sentiment.

meanings.def: to face; to answer, to reply

compositionNote: Two hand-shapes, 又 and 寸, come together as if matching palms — giving the sense of things lining up CORRECTLY.
poem: One hand (又) reaches, one hand (寸) too,
they meet up perfectly, matched and true.
When both sides fit, it must be RIGHT —
duì's the answer, clear and bright.

compositionNote: Walking (走) leads the way while 己 lends its sound — you get yourself up (RISE) and go.
poem: Legs start walking (走), self (己) in tow,
up from bed, then off you go.
Stand up straight and start to RISE —
qǐ's the moment you open your eyes.

meanings.def: not (used before 有 to negate possession)

compositionNote: Water (氵) rises with 殳 giving the sound — originally 'to sink beneath water', later borrowed for the negative NOT (HAVE).
poem: Water (氵) rises, a spear (殳) sinks deep,
swallowed whole, gone to keep.
"I have NONE" is what we say —
méi's the word when things're away.

components.meaning: a divided shape, from the radical 八
a similar-looking stroke shape used here as a simplified form, not literally 'sky'

compositionNote: 关 is a simplified graphic form (traditionally 丷+天) standing in for the original 關, which pictured a door bolted shut — hence CLOSE and CONCERN.
poem: A split latch (丷) drops down from the sky (天),
bolting the door as seasons go by.
Shut it tight, then CLOSE the gate —
guān's the bond, or lock, or fate.

compositionNote: A hand (丿) works with silk thread (糸), tying strands together into a connected SYSTEM.
poem: A hand (丿) picks up silk thread (糸) so fine,
tying each strand into a line.
Everything CONNECTS, thread to thread —
xì's the system, neatly spread.

components.meaning: originally a picture of stacked objects, later borrowed for 'again'

compositionNote: 再 is an old pictograph of something stacked or repeated, borrowed purely for its sound to mean AGAIN.

words.meaning: to talk about it later; moreover

poem: Stacked up high, one more on top,
the pile won't ever seem to stop.
Do it once, then do it AGAIN —
zài's the echo, now and then.

components.meaning: originally a pictograph of a wheat plant with ears of grain

compositionNote: 来 once drew a stalk of wheat; the picture was borrowed purely for its sound to mean 'to COME'.

words.meaning: to get up; to stand up

poem: A wheat stalk waves, ears drooping low,
swaying gently in the field's glow.
Someone's walking here, on their way —
lái means COME, arriving today.

components.meaning: a private/enclosed shape, originally an opening or cave

compositionNote: 去 once showed a person (now looking like 土) stepping away from an opening or cave (厶) — the act of LEAVING.
poem: A person (土) steps from a cave-like door (厶),
leaving footprints on the floor.
Off they wander, far away —
qù's the word for GO today.

compositionNote: A small box (口) sits inside a bigger enclosure (囗) — a spiral shape depicting a loop that turns back on itself, meaning RETURN.
poem: A box (口) inside a box (囗), round and round,
spiraling back to where it's found.
Round the loop, and RETURN you go —
huí's the circle, to and fro.

components.meaning: a horizontal stroke representing a door bolt

compositionNote: 开 abstracts an ancient picture of two hands (廾) removing the bolt (一) from a pair of doors — the act of OPENING.
poem: Two hands (廾) reach up and lift the bar (一),
swinging the door open wide and far.
Light pours in, the day's begun —
kāi means OPEN, one by one.

compositionNote: Two people (人人) sit facing each other on the ground (土) — the picture of SITTING down together.
poem: Two friends (人人) rest upon the ground (土),
no rush at all, they've settled down.
Legs crossed, backs straight, they SIT a while —
zuò's the pause, a restful style.

compositionNote: A person (亻) becomes the host (主) of a place — settling in to LIVE there.

words.meaning: to remember, to keep in mind

poem: A person (亻) becomes the host (主) at last,
settling down, the moving past.
Here's my home, where I will STAY —
zhù's the place I live each day.

components.meaning: originally a picture of a carpenter's square or tool

compositionNote: 工 is a pictograph of an ancient carpenter's square, the tool of a laborer's WORK.
poem: A carpenter's square, sturdy and true,
measures the WORK that's left to do.
Two hands, one tool, a job well done —
gōng's the labor under the sun.

compositionNote: A person (亻) suddenly (乍) sets to work — the act of MAKING or doing something.
poem: A person (亻) jumps up, suddenly (乍) keen,
to build, to craft, to MAKE a scene.
Hands get busy, ideas take shape —
zuò's the doing, no escape.

components.meaning: a hand holding a stick, action

compositionNote: A person (亻) takes old (古) materials and, with a hand's action (攵), MAKES something new — the everyday verb for doing.
poem: A person (亻) takes old (古) stuff in hand (攵),
shaping, building, as they planned.
Busy fingers, work to bake —
zuò means simply: DO or MAKE.

compositionNote: The mouth (口) opens wide next to 乞 (to beg), which lends its sound — a hungry mouth ready to EAT.
poem: A hungry mouth (口) begs (乞) for a bite,
growling loud from morning to night.
Open wide and take a seat —
chī's the word for time to EAT.

components.meaning: opposite, to turn over; sound hint

compositionNote: The food radical 饣 shows the meaning, while 反 gives the sound fǎn, softened to fàn.
poem: Food (饣) flips over (反), turned with care,
steaming rice fills up the air.
Bowl in hand, it's time to feed —
fàn's the MEAL that meets your need.

components.meaning: to pick, to gather; sound hint

compositionNote: Plants (艹) are picked (采) by hand — freshly gathered VEGETABLES ready for a dish.
poem: Green plants (艹) picked (采) fresh from the ground,
leafy bundles, crunchy and round.
Onto the plate, a tasty dish —
cài's the VEGGIE you could wish.

components.meaning: originally a picture of scattered grains of rice on a stalk

compositionNote: 米 is a pictograph showing grains of rice scattered around a central stalk, like a cross with dots.
poem: Grains scattered wide on a wooden cross,
little kernels, no husk, no loss.
Tiny bits that fill the pot —
mǐ's the RICE, a lot per lot.

compositionNote: Leaves (艹) grow above, with a person (人) resting among the trees (木) — the picture of a TEA plantation.
poem: Leaves (艹) grow high, a person (人) below,
resting calm where tea trees (木) grow.
Pick the leaves and steep them slow —
chá's the drink that helps you glow.

components.meaning: originally a picture of flowing water with ripples

compositionNote: 水 is a pictograph of a stream with swirling currents on either side.
poem: A river bends, and ripples flow,
swirling currents, watch them go.
Splash and drink, it's clear and pure —
shuǐ's the WATER, that's for sure.

compositionNote: A round fruit (田-like shape) hangs above a tree (木) — the picture of FRUIT ripening on its branch.
poem: A round fruit hangs, plump on the tree (木),
ripening sweet for you and me.
Pick it down, the FRUIT is ready —
guǒ's the harvest, plump and steady.

compositionNote: The mouth (口) does the action, while 曷 lends its sound hé, softened to hē — the mouth's job of DRINKING.
poem: A thirsty mouth (口) asks 'why not' (曷) now,
tipping the cup back, anyhow.
Gulp it down, quench the heat —
hē's to DRINK, a cool retreat.

compositionNote: Early cups were carved from wood (木), while 不 lends the sound bù, softened to bēi.
poem: Carved from wood (木), it's not (不) too small,
holding tea or water, standing tall.
Raise it high and take a sip —
bēi's the CUP you never skip.

components.meaning: to droop, to hang down; sound and sense hint

compositionNote: The eye (目) droops down (垂) as it grows heavy — the picture of drifting off to SLEEP.
poem: An eye (目) grows heavy, starts to droop (垂),
closing slow in a sleepy loop.
Drift away beneath the sheet —
shuì means SLEEP, so soft, so sweet.

meanings.def: to feel, to sense, to perceive
sleep (as in 睡觉, read jiào)

components.meaning: a cover, part of a shape shared with the top of 学 (xué, 'to study')

compositionNote: A studying, hands-and-cover shape from the top of 学 (learn) sits above 见 (to see) — perceiving and learning combine into FEELING or SENSING.
poem: Hands study hard, then open eyes (见),
learning to sense what's real, not lies.
You FEEL it deep, you understand —
jué's the sense on every hand.

components.meaning: originally a picture of a robe with a collar and two sleeves

compositionNote: 衣 is a pictograph of a robe seen from the front, with its collar at top and sleeves spreading to each side.
poem: A collar up top, two sleeves spread wide,
a robe that's ready to step inside.
Wrap it on, look sharp today —
yī's the CLOTHES you wear each day.

components.meaning: a hand pressing down a kneeling person, to subdue

compositionNote: 月 (a body, from an old boat shape) sits beside 𠬝, a hand subduing a kneeling figure, giving the idea of putting something on the body or making someone submit.
poem: A hand subdues a kneeling guy,
who dons a robe and stands close by.
The body wears what hands prepare —
CLOTHES (fú) and service, worn with care.

components.meaning: a bolt of lightning flashing down, the original picture of electricity

compositionNote: 电 is a simplified pictograph showing a flash of lightning bolting downward, the ancient symbol later used for electricity.
poem: A jagged bolt streaks through the sky,
zapping down as clouds roll by.
No plug, no wire, just raw terrain —
ELECTRICITY (diàn) sparked again!

components.meaning: strands of hair, on top of the skull
a curved shape representing the skull

compositionNote: 月 marks it as a body part, while 巛 (hair) over 匕 (a curved skull shape) pictures the head — together giving 脑, the brain.
poem: Flesh and hair atop a curve,
housing thoughts that spark and serve.
Behind your skull, ideas parade —
the BRAIN (nǎo) where all your plans are made.

components.meaning: a phonetic component from 示 (altar), giving the sound
to see — a person with a large eye

compositionNote: 见 (to see) supplies the meaning while 礻 (from 示) gives the sound shì — together, 'to look at, to view'.
poem: An altar's sign, an eye that sees,
together watching by degrees.
Point your gaze, don't look away —
to VIEW (shì) the world, come what may.

components.meaning: scenery; sunlight on a view — phonetic
three strokes depicting rays of light

compositionNote: 景 (a sunlit view, giving the sound jǐng→yǐng) is joined by 彡 (rays of light), picturing the shadow or image cast by light.
poem: Sunlit scenery casts its rays,
three light-streaks dance in golden haze.
Behind the screen, a ghostly twin —
the SHADOW (yǐng) where the light gets in.

compositionNote: 讠 (speech, from 言) combines with 舌 (tongue) — the tongue producing speech gives 话, 'words, talk'.
poem: Speech marks a tongue that wags and flaps,
chatting through the afternoon gaps.
Open your mouth, let sound cascade —
these WORDS (huà) are how connections are made.

components.meaning: tree; wood — early machines like looms were wooden

compositionNote: 木 (wood, since early machines like looms were made of wood) is paired with 几 (jī), which lends its sound, giving 机, 'machine'.
poem: A wooden stool gives up its sound,
next to timber, gears are found.
Wood and whir, a clever ploy —
the MACHINE (jī) becomes our toy.

components.meaning: a simplified picture of a bird's outstretched wings in flight

compositionNote: 飞 is a simplified pictograph showing a bird's wings spread in flight.
poem: Two wings stretched wide against the blue,
no feet on ground, just sky in view.
Up and off without delay —
to FLY (fēi) and soar and glide away.

meanings.def: a wheeled machine (e.g. 风车, windmill)

components.meaning: a simplified top-down picture of a cart with a shaft and wheel

compositionNote: 车 is a pictograph simplified from an ancient two-wheeled cart, viewed from above.
poem: A cart seen flat from up above,
wheels and shaft that workers shove.
Roll along on roads that wind —
this VEHICLE (chē) leaves feet behind.

compositionNote: 出 originally pictured a foot (止) stepping out and up from a pit or cave (凵), giving the meaning 'to go out, to emerge'.
poem: A foot climbs up and out a pit,
stepping free, not staying in it.
Leave the cave, don't hesitate —
to GO OUT (chū) and greet your fate.

components.meaning: grain; cereal plant — rent was once paid in grain

compositionNote: 禾 (grain, since rent was once paid in crops) is joined by 且 (qiě), which lends the sound, giving 租, 'to rent'.
poem: Grain once paid for borrowed land,
stacked altars help the sound expand.
Pay your due and take a stay —
to RENT (zū) a home, then move away.

compositionNote: 犭 (the animal radical) combines with 苗 (miáo), which lends its sound — together giving 猫, 'cat', whose meow echoes miáo.
poem: A furry beast beside a sprout,
seedlings growing round about.
Soft paws pad and softly meow —
the CAT (māo) is purring on the plow.

components.meaning: a bent, hooked shape — phonetic, giving the sound

compositionNote: 犭 (the dog/animal radical) pairs with 句 (jù), which lends the sound, forming 狗, 'dog'.
poem: An animal beside a hook,
bent like the shape of a shepherd's crook.
Loyal friend who barks all day —
the DOG (gǒu) who fetches and won't stray.

components.meaning: a sprout breaking through ground — part of the phonetic element
a small pellet or ball — part of the phonetic element

compositionNote: The phonetic element on top (from 埶) sits above 灬, four dots that picture flickering fire beneath — giving 热, 'hot'.
poem: A sprout and pellet, warmly grown,
fire's four dots beneath them shown.
Sweat beads form, the air's ablaze —
it's HOT (rè) on the sweltering days.

components.meaning: a command/order — phonetic, giving the sound

compositionNote: 冫 (ice) combines with 令 (lìng), which lends its sound, giving 冷, 'cold'.
poem: Two strokes of ice, so sharp and thin,
an order shouted, sound sinks in.
Shiver, shudder, wrap up tight —
it's COLD (lěng) on this frosty night.

components.meaning: raindrops falling beneath clouds in the sky

compositionNote: 雨 is a pictograph of raindrops falling from the clouds in the sky.
poem: Beneath the clouds, four droplets fall,
tapping softly on us all.
Grab a coat, don't get soaked through —
the RAIN (yǔ) is coming down on you.

meanings.def: how; why (used in 怎么, 怎样)

components.meaning: suddenly; abruptly — phonetic, giving the sound

compositionNote: 乍 (zhà) lends its sound while 心 (heart, the seat of thought) sits below, together forming 怎, used to ask 'how'.
poem: Suddenly a question stirs,
deep within the heart it whirs.
Wondering minds just want to know —
"HOW (zěn) on earth?" the questions flow.

components.meaning: wood — originally a wooden sample or pattern

compositionNote: 木 (wood, as in a wooden sample or pattern) is paired with 羊 (yáng), which lends the sound, giving 样, 'appearance; kind'.
poem: A wooden sample, carved with care,
beside a sheep with woolly hair.
Every pattern, every kind —
this APPEARANCE (yàng) shapes the mind.

components.meaning: a person/that which — phonetic, giving the sound

compositionNote: 者 (zhě) lends its sound while 阝 (the city radical, from 邑) marks a great city — together giving 都, 'all' or 'capital'.
poem: A person's shape beside a town,
a city wall that circles round.
Everyone and everything —
ALL (dōu) together, hear them sing.

meanings.def: highest; greatest (in compounds like 太阳)

components.meaning: big — a person with arms and legs spread wide
an extra dot, making 'big' even bigger

compositionNote: An extra dot (丶) added below 大 (big) makes it 'even bigger' — giving 太, 'too; extremely'.
poem: Big as big can ever be,
plus one more dot, just wait and see.
Bigger still beyond compare —
TOO (tài) much, too far, too much to bear.

components.meaning: a ticket/note — phonetic, giving the sound

compositionNote: 氵 (water) combines with 票 (piào), which lends its sound, giving 漂, 'to float' — and, by extension, light and pretty.
poem: Water ripples, calm and clear,
a ticket drifting far and near.
Bobbing gently, drifting slow —
to FLOAT (piāo) wherever currents go.

compositionNote: 亮 pictures a person (儿) standing beneath a tall structure with an opening (亠+口) that lets light shine through — giving the meaning 'bright'.
poem: A rooftop opening lets in light,
legs stand tall to catch the sight.
Glowing windows, gleaming skies —
so BRIGHT (liàng), it dazzles all our eyes.

components.meaning: a nail — phonetic, giving the sound

compositionNote: 扌 (hand) combines with 丁 (dīng, a nail), which lends its sound — a hand striking, like hammering a nail, gives 打, 'to hit'.
poem: A hand beside a sturdy nail,
hammering hard without fail.
Strike it once, then strike again —
to HIT (dǎ) it home, again and again.

meanings.def: some; a few (used after 一, 这, 那)

compositionNote: 此 (this) is topped by 二 (two), suggesting more than one of 'this' — giving 些, 'some; a few'.
poem: This very thing, but not just one,
two strokes on top make counting fun.
A pinch, a handful, not too grand —
just SOME (xiē) small pieces close at hand.

components.meaning: a simplified cursive form of 書, originally a hand (聿) holding a brush

compositionNote: 书 is a simplified cursive form of 書, which pictured a hand (聿) holding a brush to write — giving the meaning 'book; to write'.
poem: A hand once held a brush with grace,
cursive strokes now take its place.
Pages bound with tales untold —
a BOOK (shū) of stories, new and old.

components.meaning: outstanding; standing tall — phonetic, giving the sound
wood — the material a table is made of

compositionNote: 卓 (standing tall, giving the sound zhuó→zhuō) sits above 木 (wood), showing a wooden piece of furniture that stands tall — giving 桌, 'table'.
poem: Claiming space, a spot to sit,
wood below completes the fit.
Set your plate, pull up a chair —
this TABLE (zhuō) waits for you there.

components.meaning: wood — the material a chair is made of
strange; odd — phonetic, giving the sound

compositionNote: 木 (wood) combines with 奇 (qí), which lends its sound, giving 椅, 'chair'.
poem: Wood that's odd, a curious brand,
carved and shaped by skillful hand.
Rest your legs, take a seat —
this CHAIR (yǐ) makes sitting sweet.

components.meaning: an outline of a face with an eye inside

compositionNote: 面 is a pictograph of a face, showing its outline with an eye inside.
poem: An outline traced, an eye within,
the ancient picture of a chin.
Front and center, plain to see —
your FACE (miàn), as real as real can be.

components.meaning: to wrap; a bent figure enclosing something
an unborn child, curled up in the womb

compositionNote: 勹 (a wrapping, enclosing shape) surrounds 巳 (a curled-up unborn child) — the original picture of a baby wrapped in the womb, giving 包, 'to wrap; a bag'.
poem: Arms curl round a tiny form,
a baby wrapped and kept from harm.
Fold it snug and tuck it in —
this BAG (bāo) wraps up what's within.

components.meaning: originally a pictograph of a pestle, later borrowed for 'noon'

compositionNote: 午 was originally a picture of a pestle, later borrowed to represent the seventh earthly branch and the meaning 'noon', the middle point of the day.
poem: A pestle pounds from dawn's first ray,
marking time throughout the day.
Sun stands high, shadows shrink small —
it's NOON (wǔ), the midpoint of it all.

components.meaning: a simplified picture of a small low table or stool

compositionNote: 几 is a pictograph of a small low table, later borrowed to ask 'how many' or mean 'a few'.
poem: A low stool waits, both short and small,
just a seat, that's really all.
Count them up, one, two, or three —
"HOW MANY (jǐ)?" ask curiously.

meanings.def: softens a suggestion or command (e.g. 走吧, let's go)

components.meaning: mouth — shows this is a spoken particle
a snake shape — phonetic, giving the sound

compositionNote: 口 (mouth, showing this is a spoken particle) combines with 巴 (bā), which lends its sound, giving 吧, a softening tone particle.
poem: A mouth speaks out, a snake winds round,
softening every spoken sound.
Add it at the end, and hey —
it's a gentle nudge: "OKAY (ba)?"

components.meaning: a pictograph thought to show a flame or the rising sun's first ray, both linked to white light

compositionNote: 白 pictures a flame or the first ray of the rising sun, both associated with the color white.
poem: A candle's flame, a sunrise beam,
both the color white would seem.
Pure and plain, this shade so bright —
it's the color WHITE (bái), clear as light.

components.meaning: a state/nation — phonetic, giving the sound

compositionNote: 邦 (a state/nation) lends its sound above 巾 (cloth), together giving 帮, 'to help' — lending a hand like a supportive banner.
poem: A nation's name above a cloth,
lending aid, no anger, no wrath.
Lend a hand when someone's low —
to HELP (bāng) each other as we go.

components.meaning: a hand controlling a kneeling prisoner — originally judging a verdict

compositionNote: 扌 (hand) plus 𠬝 (a hand controlling a kneeling prisoner, originally 'to judge a verdict') together give 报, 'to report' — and, by extension, a newspaper that reports the news.
poem: A hand controls a kneeling one,
judging deeds till justice is done.
Now the verdict's spread today —
the REPORT (bào) reveals the way.

components.meaning: silk thread — early paper was made from fibers
clan name — phonetic, giving the sound

compositionNote: 纟 (silk thread, since early paper was made from fibers) combines with 氏 (shì), which lends its sound, giving 纸, 'paper'.
poem: Silk threads twist to form a sheet,
a family name makes the sound complete.
Write your thoughts, let ink cascade —
this PAPER (zhǐ), so thin, is made.

components.meaning: a person turned around, repeated twice in 比

compositionNote: 比 doubles the pictograph 匕 (a turned person) to show two people standing side by side, being measured against each other.
poem: Two shapes stand back to back, it's true,
each checking what the other can do.
Which one wins? Let's judge the pair —
that's how you COMPARE (bǐ) with flair.

meanings.def: don't (used before a verb as a negative command)

compositionNote: 另 (other, itself from 口+力) sits beside the knife radical 刂, as if something is cut off and set apart — hence 'other' and the idea of parting.
poem: Something other, cut apart,
sliced away with a knife (刂) so smart.
So when I shout and wave my hand,
DON'T (bié) do that — now understand?

components.meaning: an old man with long, flowing hair

compositionNote: 长 is an ancient pictograph of a person with long, flowing hair — a direct picture of length, not built from other characters.
poem: An old man's hair grows past his back,
flowing long down a windy track.
Stretch it out, don't cut it small —
that's LONG (cháng), the longest of them all.

compositionNote: The mouth 口 (semantic) sings out sounds, while the phonetic 昌 (chāng, 'flourishing') supplies the sound, giving 唱 its meaning of singing.
poem: A mouth (口) flung open, bright and bold,
two suns of sound (昌), prosperous, told.
Let your voice ring, loud and clear —
that's how you SING (chàng) for all to hear.

components.meaning: a kneeling person with an open mouth, exhaling

compositionNote: 哥 (gē, 'elder brother') supplies the sound while 欠 (a person with an open mouth) supplies the meaning of breath and voice — together, a song.
poem: Big brother (哥) opens his mouth so wide,
breath (欠) and melody swell with pride.
Every note begins to spring —
that's a SONG (gē) that makes hearts sing.

compositionNote: 巾 (cloth, originally a long garment worn habitually) is the semantic root, while 尚 (shàng, 'to esteem') lends its sound, giving 常 its sense of something constant and everyday.
poem: A cloth (巾) hung high, esteemed (尚) and true,
worn again and again, it's nothing new.
Day after day, the pattern's strong —
that's how things happen OFTEN (cháng), all along.

compositionNote: A tooth 牙 biting through a cave/hole 穴 pictures piercing all the way through — extended to mean putting a limb through cloth, i.e. wearing clothes.
poem: A tooth (牙) bites through a hole (穴) so tight,
piercing cloth from morning light.
Push your arm right through the hole —
that's how you WEAR (chuān) and reach your goal.

compositionNote: 冫 pairs with the phonetic/semantic 欠 (a person exhaling) to mark something coming after another — a time or occurrence in sequence.
poem: A cold breath (冫) yawns (欠), then yawns again,
counting moments, now and then.
One more round, then one more line —
that's another TIME (cì), the count in line.

components.meaning: a person, doubled to show one person following another

compositionNote: 从 simply doubles the pictograph 人 (a person) to show one person following behind another — the root idea of 'from' and 'to follow'.
poem: One person walks, another follows fast,
footsteps echo from the past.
Where do we begin this song?
FROM (cóng) the one who walked along.

compositionNote: 钅 (metal) is the semantic root, and 昔 (xī, 'formerly') supplies the sound; the original meaning of inlaying/mixing metal was later extended to 'wrong, mistaken'.
poem: Old metal (钅) rusted from the past (昔),
mixed up pieces, cast too fast.
Nothing here is right or strong —
that little metal spells out WRONG (cuò).

compositionNote: 亻 (person) stands beside 旦 (dàn, sunrise over the horizon), which lends its sound; 但 became a grammatical word meaning 'but'.
poem: A person (亻) waits for dawn (旦) to break,
but clouds roll in for daylight's sake.
Just when hope was bright and long —
BUT (dàn), the weather proved us wrong.

components.meaning: an arrow striking the ground, to arrive

compositionNote: 至 (an arrow striking the ground, meaning 'to arrive') combines with 刂 to reinforce the sense of reaching a destination.
poem: An arrow (至) flies and hits the ground,
sharp as a blade (刂), it makes no sound.
Straight to the target, swift and true —
that's how you ARRIVE (dào), right on cue.

meanings.def: used after a verb or adjective to link a complement of degree or possibility (de)

compositionNote: 彳 (a crossroads, 'to walk') combines with a hand 寸 reaching for a shell-like object, picturing someone acquiring something while on the move — 'to get'.
poem: Walking (彳) far with a hand (寸) that gropes,
reaching for shells and distant hopes.
Step by step, the prize is met —
that's how you GET (dé) what you have set.

compositionNote: 竹 (bamboo strips, used for sorting and counting) sits above 寺 (sì, 'temple', here a phonetic), giving the sense of orderly ranks — and of waiting one's turn.
poem: Bamboo strips (竹), stacked outside the gate,
counted slow by the temple (寺) gate.
Patience grows as minutes pass along —
that's how you WAIT (děng), all day long.

meanings.def: prefix forming ordinal numbers (e.g. 第一, first)

compositionNote: 竹 (bamboo slips used for numbering) is semantic, and 弟 (dì, 'younger brother') lends its sound, producing the ordinal-number marker 第.
poem: Bamboo slips (竹), numbered one by one,
little brother (弟) counts till done.
First, then second, all in a row —
ORDINAL (dì) markers, now you know.

components.meaning: a cord wound around a stick in even, ordered loops

compositionNote: 弟 is an ancient pictograph of a cord wound around a stick in ordered loops — 'in sequence' came to mean the younger sibling, who comes after in birth order.
poem: A cord wound round a stick with care,
in perfect order, layer by layer.
Born after me, but still so dear —
my YOUNGER BROTHER (dì), always near.

compositionNote: 忄 (heart/mind) is semantic, while 董 (dǒng, 'to supervise') supplies the sound, giving 懂 its meaning of grasping something mentally.
poem: A heart (忄) that watches, keeping guard (董),
catching meaning, working hard.
Click! The lightbulb starts to glow —
now you UNDERSTAND (dǒng), now you know.

meanings.def: to act; to start doing something

components.meaning: a simplified shape (from 重), used here only for its form

compositionNote: The simplified top part (a modified form of 重) combines with 力 (strength/power) to show that motion requires force.
poem: Clouds (云) drift by with silent grace,
but power (力) pushes them through space.
Nothing stays still, nothing's fixed —
that's how things MOVE (dòng), in motion mixed.

compositionNote: 户 (a door) is semantic, and 方 (fāng, 'square/direction') lends its sound, giving 房 its meaning of a house or room.
poem: A door (户) stands square (方), facing the street,
a shelter built for tired feet.
Walls around and roof above —
that's a HOUSE (fáng), a room to love.

compositionNote: Sunlight 日 shining through a gate 门 pictures the gap or space between two things, later extended to mean a room.
poem: Sunlight (日) sneaks through a gate (门) ajar,
slipping in from near and far.
The light divides what's seen and unseen —
that's the gap called ROOM (jiān), the in-between.

components.meaning: two wings spread apart, facing opposite directions

compositionNote: 非 pictures two wings spread apart in opposite directions, an image of things that don't align — hence its meaning 'not'.
poem: Two wings spread out, turned opposite ways,
flying apart through separate days.
Nothing matches, nothing's the same —
that's NOT (fēi), the opposite claim.

compositionNote: 贝 (a cowrie shell, ancient currency) is semantic, and 化 (huà, 'to change') lends its sound, giving 货 its meaning of goods traded for money.
poem: Shells (贝) once used to trade and change (化),
bought and sold on the market range.
Boxes stacked on every shelf —
that's the GOODS (huò), for sale itself.

components.meaning: an ancient curled pictographic shape, related to 己

compositionNote: 已 is an ancient, simplified pictographic form related to 己, whose original picture is unclear; it was borrowed for the abstract sense of 'already'.
poem: A curling shape, coiled and done,
its story told, its journey run.
Look back now — the deed is set —
that's ALREADY (yǐ), no more to fret.

components.meaning: simplified from 巠, underground water threading its way (phonetic)

compositionNote: 纟 (silk thread) is semantic, and the right side (a simplified form of 巠, depicting underground water threading its way) lends the sound, giving 经 the sense of a thread running through — to pass through, or manage.

words.meaning: to pass through; to go by

poem: Silk threads (纟) run like water below (巠),
weaving straight, a steady flow.
Follow the path where the thread has spread —
that's how you PASS THROUGH (jīng), thread by thread.

compositionNote: 京 (jīng, 'capital', a picture of a tall building) combines with 尤 (yóu, 'especially/outstanding') to give the sense of moving right up to something — 'then, at once'.
poem: Near the capital (京), especially (尤) grand,
straight to the palace, close at hand.
No delay, no waiting spell —
THEN (jiù) it happens, right and well.

compositionNote: 耂 (the 'old' radical, from 老) combines with 丂 (a bent breath escaping, phonetic) to give 考 its sound and its meaning of examining or testing.
poem: An old man (耂) breathes (丂) a heavy sigh,
questions loom as the clock ticks by.
Pencils ready, minds engaged —
time to take the TEST (kǎo), turn the page.

compositionNote: 讠 (speech) is semantic, and 式 (shì, 'pattern/style') lends its sound, giving 试 its meaning of trying something out.
poem: Words (讠) laid out in a patterned (式) frame,
practice rounds before the game.
Give it a go, don't be shy —
that's how you TRY (shì), give it a try.

compositionNote: 口 (mouth) beside 丂 (a bent breath escaping) pictures an approving vocal sound — the origin of 可's meaning 'can, may'.
poem: A mouth (口) breathes out (丂) a sound of yes,
approving nods without distress.
Permission granted, nothing's barred —
you CAN (kě) proceed, the path's not hard.

compositionNote: 讠 (spoken/taught words) is semantic, and 果 (guǒ, 'fruit/result') lends its sound, giving 课 its meaning of a lesson or class.
poem: Words (讠) are spoken, ripe as fruit (果),
lessons growing from the root.
Open your book, the bell will ring —
time for CLASS (kè), let learning sing.

compositionNote: 忄 (heart) is semantic, and 夬 (guài, 'to decide/break off') lends its sound, giving 快 its senses of being quick and of feeling pleased.
poem: A heart (忄) decides (夬) in a single beat,
racing forward, light and fleet.
Quick as lightning, feeling grand —
FAST and HAPPY (kuài), hand in hand.

components.meaning: a simplified picture of a stringed wooden instrument

compositionNote: 乐 is a simplified pictograph derived from an ancient drawing of a wooden instrument strung with silk cords — music, and by extension, joy.
poem: A tiny instrument, strings that hum,
joyful music, here it comes.
Smiles arrive, no room for gloom —
that's HAPPY (lè), filling up the room.

components.meaning: field, here pictured as a stacked bundle

compositionNote: 田 sits above 糸 (silk thread), picturing bundles piled up and tied together — a heavy load that leaves one tired.
poem: Bundles of thread (糸) stacked on the field (田),
piled up high, a heavy yield.
Carry it all, your legs go weak —
now you're TIRED (lèi), too worn to speak.

components.meaning: a simplified pictograph related to a bird caught, then released from a net

compositionNote: 离 is a simplified pictograph, historically related to a bird caught then let loose from a net — capturing the idea of separating and leaving.
poem: A bird once caught, now flies up high,
leaving the net, into the sky.
Distance grows between here and there —
that's how you LEAVE (lí), gone through the air.

components.meaning: an ancient balance scale with two pans

compositionNote: 两 pictures an old balance scale with two pans hanging in matched pairs — the origin of its meaning 'two, a pair'.
poem: A balance scale with pans that sway,
one on each side, equal weigh.
Never alone, always a pair —
that's the number TWO (liǎng), balanced fair.

compositionNote: 足 (foot) is semantic, and 各 (gè, 'each') lends its sound, giving 路 its meaning of the road each traveler's feet wear down.
poem: Feet (足) march on, each (各) step the same,
wearing paths without a name.
Follow it far, follow it wide —
that's the ROAD (lù), your walking guide.

components.meaning: people following the banner (appears twice in the original pictograph)

compositionNote: 方 pictures a fluttering banner, and the remaining strokes picture people (人) following behind it — the original image of a company of travelers marching under a flag.
poem: A banner (方) waves, held up with pride,
people (人) follow, side by side.
Marching onward, near and far —
that's to TRAVEL (lǚ), wherever you are.

components.meaning: a flag fluttering as someone walks (phonetic)

compositionNote: Water (氵) plus 斿, a fluttering banner that also lends its sound — together they picture drifting through water or roaming free.
poem: Water swirls where banners fly,
a flag held high as rivers ply.
Dive in, drift on, roam and go —
to SWIM and ROAM (yóu), with the flow.

compositionNote: A heart (忄) stretched long and graceful (曼) — a mind unhurried gives the meaning of SLOW, and 曼 also supplies the sound.
poem: Heart stretched long and full of grace,
takes its time at easy pace.
No rush at all, just calm and low —
SLOW (màn) as syrup, sweet and slow.

compositionNote: A heart (忄) that feels it has lost (亡) itself in too many tasks — a flustered mind gives the meaning BUSY.
poem: Heart that feels it's lost its way,
too many tasks to fit the day.
Rushing here, rushing there, no rest at all —
so BUSY (máng), answering every call.

components.meaning: an extra stroke on top, like a hairpin

compositionNote: Built from the picture of a mother (母) with an ornament on top, extended in meaning to stand for any one, and so EVERY one.
poem: A mother-shape with hairpin bright,
stands for one, and stands for right.
From her comes each, and all the same —
EVERY (měi) single one, by any name.

compositionNote: A woman (女) who is not yet (未) fully grown — the younger girl of the family, the YOUNGER SISTER.
poem: A girl who's not yet grown so tall,
littlest sibling, loved by all.
Younger, sweeter, trailing behind —
YOUNGER SISTER (mèi), one of a kind.

components.meaning: a two-leaf door, drawn as a picture

compositionNote: A simple picture of a two-panel door swinging on its frame gives the character DOOR.
poem: Two wooden leaves stand side by side,
a picture of a door thrown wide.
Knock and enter, come on in —
that's the DOOR (mén) where trips begin.

meanings.def: for long, thin things (roads, fish, trousers)

components.meaning: simplified top, from the older phonetic 攸

compositionNote: A tree (木) with a slender branch on top — something long and thin, giving the measure word for STRIPS and long items.
poem: A tree with a slender branch that grows,
one long strip, as thin as it goes.
Count them out, one by one, so neat —
a STRIP (tiáo) of noodles, or a street.

compositionNote: A woman (女) paired with the sound-carrying 乃 gives 奶 — originally the woman who nurses a child, hence MILK.
poem: A woman says her sound so plain (乃),
pouring milk again, again.
Grandma smiles and fills the cup —
that's the MILK (nǎi), warm, drink it up.

meanings.def: male; man (used attributively, e.g. 男人, 男孩)

compositionNote: Strength (力) applied in the field (田) — the ancient picture of a man working the land gives the meaning MALE.
poem: In the field he lends his strength,
plowing rows at any length.
Muscle, sweat, and labor's call —
that's a MALE (nán), standing tall.

compositionNote: A hand (又) trying to catch a bird (隹) — a slippery, hard-to-grasp task, the picture of DIFFICULT.
poem: A hand that chases a fleeing bird,
tricky catch, and rarely heard.
Hard to grasp and hard to do —
that's DIFFICULT (nán), through and through.

compositionNote: You (你) plus a heart (心) beneath — speaking to someone with heartfelt respect gives the polite YOU.
poem: "You" plus a heart laid at the base,
warmth and manners, gentle grace.
Speak with respect, in kindest tone —
that's the polite word YOU (nín) alone.

components.meaning: an ox's head with horns, seen from the front

compositionNote: A simple pictograph of an ox's head and horns gives the character OX.
poem: Two horns atop a sturdy head,
a picture from the barn instead.
Pulling plows through muddy fields —
that's the OX (niú), whose labor yields.
