components.meaning: top element, historically suggesting broad or general

compositionNote: A broad, general shape sitting above 方 (direction) narrows down to a nearby direction — the meaning SIDE.
poem: Wide and broad, spread far and free,
beside a direction you will see.
Not the center, just nearby —
that's the SIDE (páng), close passing by.

compositionNote: Walking (辶) along a boundary, with the simplified 力 standing in for the original sound component, gives EDGE or SIDE.
poem: Walking on, with strength in tow,
tracing borders as you go.
Along the rim, along the line —
that's the EDGE (biān), the border's sign.

compositionNote: A foot (足) in motion, paired with the sound-carrying 包, gives the action of legs pounding forward — to RUN.
poem: Feet that wrap around the track,
racing forward, no turning back.
Fast and fleet, with pounding sound —
to RUN (pǎo) is to cover ground.

compositionNote: Two footprints stacked one after another, left then right, form the picture of a single STEP.
poem: One foot down, then one foot more,
footprints stacking on the floor.
Left then right, then right then left —
a single STEP (bù), one foot's heft.

compositionNote: A person (亻) who adapts and changes (更) with ease — quick to adjust, hence CONVENIENT.
poem: A person who will change with ease,
adapting fast to any breeze.
Handy, simple, quick to do —
CONVENIENT (biàn) fits right for you.

components.meaning: a table with meat on it (original picture)

compositionNote: Under a roof (宀), a table set just right (且) shows the proper, fitting amount — the meaning SUITABLE.
poem: Under a roof, a table spread,
just the right amount is said.
Fitting well, appropriate too —
SUITABLE (yí) is right for you.

compositionNote: A western (覀) sign posted like an altar notice (示) — an official paper slip, the TICKET or ballot.
poem: West winds blow past an altar sign,
a paper stub, a printed line.
Show it quick before you board —
that's your TICKET (piào), safely stored.

compositionNote: A hand arranging hair above a woman (女) — the picture of a woman managing the household, the WIFE.
poem: A hand pins up her flowing hair,
a woman with a household's care.
Bound by vows, she stands close by —
that's the WIFE (qī), 'neath the sky.

compositionNote: Wood (木) framed under a shelter (广) — a wooden frame for resting, the picture of a BED.
poem: Under a shelter, wood laid flat,
a cozy frame to rest upon that.
Tuck in tight when day is done —
that's your BED (chuáng), when night's begun.

compositionNote: A single stroke standing atop 十 (ten) suggests ten taken many times over — the number THOUSAND.
poem: A person stands atop the ten,
multiplied again, again.
Hundreds stacked, then stacked some more —
a THOUSAND (qiān), that's the score.

compositionNote: The sun (日) shining alongside 青 (clear blue-green) gives the meaning SUNNY, with 青 also lending the sound.
poem: The sun shines on skies of blue,
clear and bright, no clouds in view.
Warm rays fall on everything —
that's a SUNNY (qíng) day in spring.

compositionNote: A word (讠) spoken to raise (上) someone else up or ahead — giving way with speech, the meaning to LET or ALLOW.
poem: Words spoken, rising up with grace,
stepping back to give you space.
"After you," is what they say —
to LET (ràng) someone lead the way.

compositionNote: A roof (宀) over a wide valley (谷) — plenty of space to hold things, giving the meaning to CONTAIN or allow.
poem: Under a roof, a valley wide,
plenty of room for all inside.
Space to hold, and room to spare —
to CONTAIN (róng) with ease and care.

components.meaning: do not (bottom, remnant of the same pictograph)

compositionNote: Originally a picture of a changeable lizard, the simplified shape reads as sun (日) over 勿 — something that shifts smoothly and effortlessly, hence EASY.
poem: Sun above, a "don't" below,
nothing hard, just letting go.
Simple steps that flow with ease —
EASY (yì) as a gentle breeze.

components.meaning: a human torso, drawn from the side

compositionNote: A pictograph of a person's torso, seen from the side, gives the character BODY.
poem: A curving shape, a torso whole,
the picture of a body's role.
Arms and legs and beating heart —
that's the BODY (shēn), every part.

compositionNote: A person (亻) and their root or foundation (本) — the basic frame that holds a person together, the BODY.
poem: A person's root, their very core,
the frame that holds them, nothing more.
Strong and whole from head to feet —
that's the BODY (tǐ), form complete.

compositionNote: The sickness radical (疒), showing a person lying ill, combined with the sound-carrying 丙, gives the meaning ILLNESS.
poem: A sickbed shape with 丙 hidden deep,
fever rising, troubled sleep.
Aches and chills, you're feeling low —
you're SICK (bìng), and germs will show.

components.meaning: a hand with fingers and wrist, drawn as a picture

compositionNote: A simple pictograph of an open hand with its fingers gives the character HAND.
poem: Five fingers spread out on a palm,
a simple picture, still and calm.
Reach and hold, and wave hello —
that's the HAND (shǒu), watch it go.

components.meaning: fur; hair (top, now merged into the shape)

compositionNote: Originally fur (毛) worn on the outside of clothing (衣) — the visible surface of a garment, extended to mean what is shown on the outside: to EXPRESS, or a watch face.
poem: Fur worn outside over clothes,
showing what the surface shows.
A dial worn upon the wrist —
to SHOW or WATCH (biǎo), don't be missed.

meanings.def: to see someone off; to deliver

components.meaning: shape resembling a gate or pass (phonetic remnant)

compositionNote: Walking (辶) someone through the gate (关) and beyond — accompanying them out, or carrying a gift along the way, giving TO SEND or GIVE.
poem: Walking on, with a gift in hand,
delivered forth across the land.
A present given, a friend seen off —
to GIVE or SEND (sòng), never scoff.

compositionNote: A mouth (口) speaking up despite the small insect (虫) — voicing an objection anyway, the sense of ALTHOUGH.
poem: A mouth that speaks despite the bug,
"but still," it says, with a knowing shrug.
Yes, but — despite it, all the same —
ALTHOUGH (suī) begins the frame.

meanings.def: suffix forming adverbs; so; like that

compositionNote: Meat (月) from a dog (犬) set over fire (灬) — originally 'to burn', later borrowed to mean SO or LIKE THAT.
poem: Dog meat set above the fire,
burning bright and climbing higher.
"Just like that," is what we say —
SO, LIKE THAT (rán), it happened that way.

compositionNote: A foot (足) swinging with the sound-carrying 易 — a quick strike of the foot gives the meaning to KICK.
poem: A foot that finds it easy, quick,
swinging hard to give a kick.
Ball goes flying, goal in sight —
to KICK (tī) it well with all your might.

components.meaning: a leg with knee above and foot below, drawn as a picture

compositionNote: A pictograph of a leg bent at the knee down to the foot gives the character FOOT, later extended to mean ENOUGH.
poem: A knee above, a foot below,
a leg's whole picture, head to toe.
Plenty here, no need for more —
ENOUGH, a FOOT (zú), this word's the core.

components.meaning: to seek (phonetic, gives the sound qiú)

compositionNote: Jade (王) shows balls were once precious round stones, while 求 lends the sound qiú.
poem: A king (王) went out to seek (求) some fun,
He chased a BALL (qiú) beneath the sun,
Round and bouncy, jade-bright gleam,
Kick it, throw it, join the team!

components.meaning: head; page (semantic, related to a heading)

compositionNote: 页 (head/page) shows this is about a heading or title, while 是 contributes a sound close to tí.
poem: Is (是) it right? Turn the page (页) to see,
A tricky TOPIC (tí) waits for thee,
Questions written line by line,
Answer well and you'll be fine!

meanings.def: to jump; to leap; to bounce

compositionNote: The foot (足) does the moving while 兆 supplies the sound tiào.
poem: Feet (足) sense an omen (兆), start to spring,
They JUMP (tiào) and leap at anything,
Up and over, quick and light,
Hopping high from morn to night!

components.meaning: originally a picture of a dancer holding streamers
two feet pointing opposite ways (semantic, movement of feet)

compositionNote: The top once pictured a dancer with flowing sleeves; once that shape was borrowed to mean 'not have', 舛 (feet) was added to keep the meaning of dancing.
poem: A dancer twirled with silk in hand,
Two feet (舛) kept time across the land,
Swirl and sway, the DANCE (wǔ) unfolds,
A story that the body holds!

components.meaning: first; origin (phonetic, gives the sound wán)

compositionNote: A roof (宀) over 元 suggests a house brought to completion, with 元 also hinting at the sound wán.
poem: Under the roof (宀), from first (元) to end,
The work is FINISHED (wán), time to spend,
Every task now closed and done,
Roof stands proud when day is won!

components.meaning: first; origin (phonetic, gives the sound wán)

compositionNote: Jade (王) suggests fiddling with a gem for amusement, while 元 gives the sound wán.
poem: A prince (王) with jewels, first (元) of all,
Loves to PLAY (wán) and have a ball,
Toys and games from dawn to dark,
Every jade gem sparks a spark!

components.meaning: to avoid (phonetic, gives the sound wǎn)

compositionNote: The sun (日) low in the sky marks evening, while 免 lends the sound wǎn.
poem: The sun (日) tries to avoid (免) the night,
But EVENING (wǎn) comes, dimming light,
Late and slow the day retires,
Stars replace the sun's own fires.

components.meaning: master (phonetic, gives a sound close to wǎng)

compositionNote: Walking steps (彳) show motion toward somewhere, while 主 contributes the sound.
poem: Steps (彳) march on, the master's (主) way,
Heading TOWARD (wǎng) the break of day,
Past roads walked and paths ahead,
Onward still, by feet we're led.

meanings.def: to do; to act as; to become

components.meaning: originally a hand leading an elephant, picturing 'to do work'

compositionNote: The simplified form no longer shows its parts clearly; it comes from an old picture of a hand guiding an elephant to work.
poem: A hand once led an elephant near,
To DO (wéi), to act — the sense is clear,
It stands for tasks both big and small,
One little word that means it all.

components.meaning: to lose; to perish (phonetic, gives the sound wàng)

compositionNote: Something lost (亡) from the heart (心) is quite literally forgotten.
poem: Something's lost (亡) inside the heart (心),
Memories that fall apart,
To FORGET (wàng) what once we knew,
Slips away like morning dew.

compositionNote: A mouth (口) at the door (门) calls out to ask something, with 门 also lending the sound.
poem: Knock the door (门), open your mouth (口) wide,
ASK (wèn) a question, step inside,
Curious minds will always seek,
Answers found for those who speak.

components.meaning: a picture of a vine with a melon hanging from it

compositionNote: A single pictograph showing a melon dangling on its curling vine.
poem: A curling vine, a dangling round,
A juicy MELON (guā) on the ground,
Sweet and cool on summer days,
Vines twist round in curly ways.

components.meaning: crossed lines (semantic, a sparse, loose weave)

compositionNote: Loosely crossed threads (爻) on cloth (巾) picture a sparse weave, extended to mean something rare — hence hoped for.
poem: Threads cross and weave upon the cloth (巾),
A sparse design, both fine and soft,
We HOPE (xī) for dreams that rarely come,
Rare as thread that's finely spun.

meanings.def: to look toward; to gaze into the distance

components.meaning: to lose; gone (phonetic hint, gives the sound wàng)

compositionNote: Someone gazes up at the moon (月) longing for what is gone (亡), the origin of both 'to gaze' and 'to hope'.
poem: Lost (亡) at night, we watch the moon (月),
And HOPE (wàng) the morning comes real soon,
Gazing far past hill and tree,
Wishing for what eyes can't see.

compositionNote: Water (氵) does the washing, while 先 lends its sound to xǐ.
poem: Water (氵) flows to go first (先) of all,
To WASH (xǐ) away both dirt and squall,
Scrub your hands and rinse them clean,
Freshest start you've ever seen.

components.meaning: bamboo (semantic, bending like laughter bends the body)

compositionNote: Bamboo (竹) bending in the wind is likened to a body bent over with laughter (夭).
poem: Bamboo (竹) leans and bends with glee (夭),
We LAUGH (xiào) so hard, we bend our knee,
Giggles rustle just like leaves,
Joy that bamboo swaying weaves.

components.meaning: dear; parent (phonetic, gives the sound xīn)

compositionNote: An axe (斤) cutting fresh wood gives the idea of newness, while 亲 lends the sound xīn.
poem: A dear one (亲) chops wood with an axe (斤),
Fresh planks emerge from ancient stacks,
Something NEW (xīn) begins to form,
Bright and different, freshly born.

components.meaning: woman (semantic, ancient clans traced through mothers)
to be born (phonetic-semantic, gives sound and sense of lineage)

compositionNote: A woman (女) giving birth (生) reflects how ancient surnames were originally passed down through mothers' clans.
poem: A woman (女) gives birth (生) to a name,
Passed through lines from whence they came,
Your SURNAME (xìng) tells your family tree,
Roots that trace through history.

compositionNote: A person (亻) leaning against a tree (木) pictures the very act of resting.
poem: A person (亻) leans against a tree (木),
Taking time to REST (xiū) so free,
Shade above and grass below,
Napping where the breezes blow.

components.meaning: nose (semantic, originally a picture of a nose, source of breath)

compositionNote: Breath from the nose (自) reaching the heart (心) pictures breathing and, by extension, resting.
poem: The nose (自) breathes deep, the heart (心) beats slow,
A quiet BREATH (xī) begins to flow,
Rest a while and catch your air,
Peaceful moments everywhere.

components.meaning: a hand or broom (originally used to sweep snow, semantic hint)

compositionNote: Rain (雨) that turns cold falls as snow, with the lower part once picturing a hand sweeping it away.
poem: Rain (雨) turns cold, a hand (彐) will sweep,
White SNOW (xuě) falls in drifts so deep,
Flakes come dancing from the sky,
Blanket fields as winter's nigh.

components.meaning: an accomplished man (phonetic, gives a sound close to yán)

compositionNote: 页 (head) points to the face, whose expression and hue give this character its meanings of face and color; 彦 lends the sound.
poem: A noble man (彦) shows his head (页) with pride,
His COLORFUL (yán) face he can't hide,
Every hue upon his cheek,
Tells the story words can't speak.

components.meaning: originally two figures side by side, picturing a facial expression or complexion

compositionNote: An old picture of a person's complexion or mood, later generalized to mean 'color'.
poem: Two figures bend in shifting hue,
A COLOR (sè) shows a mood or two,
Red for joy and blue for calm,
Every shade an ancient charm.

components.meaning: eye (semantic, a picture of an eye)
to stop; firm (phonetic, gives the sound yǎn)

compositionNote: 目 (eye) carries the meaning, while 艮 supplies the sound yǎn.
poem: An eye (目) stands firm and will not budge (艮),
The EYE (yǎn) that watches, does not fudge,
Windows to the soul they say,
Seeing all both night and day.

compositionNote: 目 (eye) gives the meaning of eyeball, while 青 lends the sound jīng.
poem: An eye (目) so bright, like green-blue skies (青),
The EYEBALL (jīng) sparkles, never lies,
Paired with 眼 to make a stare,
Dot the dragon's eye with care.

components.meaning: a picture of a sheep's head with curving horns

compositionNote: A pictograph of a sheep's head, seen from the front with its curved horns.
poem: Two curving horns upon a head,
A woolly SHEEP (yáng) in pasture led,
Baa and graze from morn to dusk,
Fluffy white in fields of musk.

components.meaning: a picture of a cross-section of meat with muscle lines

compositionNote: A pictograph showing a slice of meat with the lines of its muscle or ribs.
poem: A slice with lines like ribs inside,
Fresh MEAT (ròu) upon the chopping side,
Sizzle, grill it, stew it too,
Dinner's ready, made for you.

components.meaning: to agree; approximately (phonetic, gives the sound yào)

compositionNote: Herbs (艹) form the basis of medicine, while 约 lends its sound to yào.
poem: Herbs (艹) agreed upon (约) with care,
Brewed as MEDICINE (yào) to share,
Bitter sips to make you well,
Nature's cure in leaf and shell.

components.meaning: originally a picture of a curling snake or ladle, later borrowed as a grammar word

compositionNote: An ancient pictograph whose original picture was borrowed purely for its sound to write the grammatical word 'also'.
poem: A curling snake once slid this way,
Now means 'ALSO' (yě) in what we say,
Me too, you too, and him as well,
A tiny word with much to tell.

compositionNote: A sound (音) rising from the heart (心) captures an inner meaning or intention.
poem: A sound (音) rings out straight from the heart (心),
An IDEA (yì) starts to take its part,
Meaning hidden, feeling deep,
Thoughts the mind will always keep.

components.meaning: field-like shape, actually a simplified form of 囟 (skull/fontanelle)

compositionNote: The top part looks like a field (田) but is really a worn-down form of 囟 (the skull), combined with 心 (heart) to represent thinking with mind and heart together.
poem: The brain (囟, like a field 田) and heart (心) combine,
To THINK (sī) and ponder, thoughts align,
Ideas grow like crops in rows,
Wisdom blooms where thinking grows.

meanings.def: yin (the shady, feminine principle, opposite of yang)

components.meaning: mound; hill (semantic, the shady side of a hill)
moon (semantic, associated with darkness and yin)

compositionNote: The shady side of a hill (阝) paired with the moon (月) pictures shade, cloudiness, and the yin principle.
poem: The shady mound (阝), the pale moon's (月) glow,
OVERCAST (yīn) skies, the sun lies low,
Yin and shadow, dim and cool,
Nature's balance, nature's rule.

components.meaning: big; a person (semantic, a person resting on a mat)

compositionNote: A person (大) resting inside an enclosure or mat (囗) originally meant 'to rely on', which extended to mean the cause one relies on.
poem: A person (大) rests inside a mat (囗),
BECAUSE (yīn) of comfort found in that,
Every cause has its own seed,
Reasons planted, thoughts proceed.

components.meaning: forever (phonetic, gives the sound yǒng, originally a picture of a long flowing stream)

compositionNote: Water (氵) plus 永, which originally pictured a long branching stream, together give 'to swim'.
poem: Water (氵) flows on forever (永) still,
We SWIM (yǒng) with strokes and steady will,
Kick and glide beneath the waves,
Forever flowing, water's ways.

compositionNote: A hand (又) helping the mouth (口) reflects that most people use their right hand to eat, giving 'right side' its meaning.
poem: A hand (又) once helped to feed the mouth (口),
The RIGHT (yòu) side, strong from north to south,
Most of us reach with this same hand,
The right side helps us understand.

components.meaning: a picture of a fish with head, body, and tail

compositionNote: A pictograph of a fish, viewed from the side with its head, scaled body, and tail.
poem: A fish's fins, a fish's tail,
Swimming fast, it will not fail,
FISH (yú) that swim in streams and seas,
Gliding past with silver ease.

compositionNote: 元 (yuán) lends its sound while 辶 (walking) adds the idea of travel, together picturing a road that stretches far away.
poem: Feet (辶) keep walking, mile by mile,
元 lends the sound to make it worthwhile,
the road runs on past hill and pier,
FAR (yuǎn) is the place that's never near.

compositionNote: 辶 (movement) combines with 云 (yún, cloud) as a sound hint, picturing things carried along like drifting clouds — to transport, and by extension, the drifting turns of fate.
poem: Clouds (云) drift by, and feet (辶) must roam,
carrying loads far away from home,
fortune shifts like weather in the sky,
LUCK and MOVE (yùn) go drifting by.

compositionNote: The sun (日) rising above a sprouting plant (十) shows the very first light of day.
poem: Sun (日) peeks up over a little sprout (十),
the day begins without a doubt,
roosters crow and no more snore,
EARLY (zǎo) light knocks at the door.

meanings.def: a unit of length, about 3.33 meters
(in 丈夫) husband; (in 岳丈) father-in-law

compositionNote: Originally a hand (又) holding a ten-chi (十) measuring rod, 丈 named the unit of length and, by extension, a grown man — the 'husband' in 丈夫.
poem: A hand (又) grips a measuring rod of ten (十),
stretched out long to mark it then,
a grown man tall, a household head,
a ZHANG (zhàng) of length, or the man you wed.

components.meaning: a person, arms and legs spread wide
a hairpin worn by an adult man

compositionNote: A grown person (大) wearing a hairpin (一) across the head marks an adult man — hence 'husband' or 'man'.
poem: A person (大) stands with arms out wide,
a hairpin (一) crowns him, full of pride,
a man grown up, a household's chief,
HUSBAND (fū) — short in strokes, but not belief.

compositionNote: A hand (扌) reaching out, with 戈 (gē) lending its sound, pictures the act of searching for something.
poem: A hand (扌) reaches out, patting around,
戈 hums the sound but stays unfound,
under the bed, behind the door,
SEARCH (zhǎo) until you find some more.

meanings.def: used after a verb to show an ongoing action or state (-ing)
(read zháo) to touch, to catch, to fall asleep

compositionNote: 着 comes from 著: a shepherd's watchful eye (目) upon the flock (羊, abbreviated), extended to mean 'attached to, ongoing' as the aspect particle zhe.
poem: A shepherd's eye (目) watches the sheep (羊) all day,
attached, ongoing, they can't stray,
the action keeps on, verb plus ZHE,
still going strong, still on its way.

compositionNote: An eye (目) set atop a solid stand (十 and 八-shaped legs) pictures something examined closely and found solid and unchanging — hence 'true, real'.
poem: An eye (目) set high on sturdy legs (八),
steady as ten (十) — nothing sags,
look close and see it's not a lie,
TRULY (zhēn) real, no need to pry.

meanings.def: exactly; just (indicating an action in progress)

components.meaning: a line, a target or standard

compositionNote: A foot (止) walking straight up to a line (一) shows heading directly toward the standard — 'correct, exactly'.
poem: A foot (止) steps straight up to the line (一),
no wobble left, no curve, all fine,
aimed dead center, hitting true,
CORRECT (zhèng) is what a straight foot'll do.

compositionNote: Words from the mouth (口) fly straight and swift as an arrow (矢) — speaking with the sureness of knowledge.
poem: An arrow (矢) flies straight and true,
words from the mouth (口) fly swift there too,
an answer sure, no doubt or lack,
to KNOW (zhī) is to hit the fact.

compositionNote: A head (首) leading the way while feet (辶) walk forward pictures a road, and by extension, 'the Way' one speaks of or follows.
poem: A head (首) leads, feet (辶) walk behind,
tracing a road for the following mind,
a path, a word, a truth to say,
THE WAY (dào) opens, day by day.

compositionNote: 冫 hints at a level standard (like still water) while 隹 (a bird) lends the sound, together giving 'accurate, precise' and 'to allow'.
poem: Still water's level (冫) never lies,
a bird (隹) lends sound as it flies,
hit the mark, don't miss the run,
ACCURATE (zhǔn) and precisely done.

components.meaning: a foot stepping down; to go

compositionNote: 备 is a simplified, cursive-derived form of 備; its two visible parts, 夂 (going) over 田 (field), carry forward the older sense of stocking and getting things ready.
poem: Slow steps (夂) cross a field (田) with care,
gathering all that's needed there,
stock the shelf, don't leave it bare,
PREPARE (bèi) — have it ready to share.

components.meaning: a running person swinging their arms (not 'earth' here)

compositionNote: A person swinging their arms (the top, now shaped like 土) above a foot (止) pictures someone in motion — to walk or go.
poem: Arms swing wide (土), a foot (止) steps out,
marching forward without a doubt,
down the street and round about,
to WALK (zǒu) is what it's all about.

components.meaning: to say (a worn-down form of an old 'roof' shape)
to take, grasp (itself an ear 耳 seized by a hand 又)

compositionNote: 曰 (say) sits above 取 (to take) — taking hold of the very best of what is spoken of, the idea behind 'most'.
poem: Say (曰) it loud, then take (取) the crown,
grab the prize of best renown,
top of the heap, wearing the crest,
MOST (zuì) of all — simply the best.

compositionNote: A hand (𠂇) reaching for a tool (工) pictures the left hand assisting the right one in work — hence 'left'.
poem: A hand (𠂇) reaches for a tool (工) nearby,
helping out, no need to ask why,
turn that way, not to the right,
LEFT (zuǒ) hand steady, holding tight.

compositionNote: 纟 (silk) shows the material being dyed, while 工 (gōng) lends the sound — cloth dyed a bright red.
poem: Silk threads (纟) dyed a brilliant hue,
工 hums the sound, and now it's true,
lanterns glow and cheeks feel warm,
RED (hóng) as fire in every form.

compositionNote: 火 is a pictograph of leaping flames, its two side strokes like sparks thrown off the fire.
poem: Flames leap up, both wild and bright,
dancing tongues of orange light,
crackling loud through the night so raw,
FIRE (huǒ) — the oldest thing we saw.

compositionNote: 立 (to stand) plus 占 (zhàn, to occupy, also lending the sound) pictures someone standing and holding their spot — a stop or station.
poem: Stand up straight (立) and claim your spot (占),
占 hums the sound, this is the plot,
wait right here, don't roam too far,
the STATION (zhàn) is where you are.

meanings.def: (read jiào) teaching; religion, as in 宗教

components.meaning: crossed lines, patterns to be studied
a hand holding a stick, to urge action

compositionNote: Patterns to learn (爻) are shown to a child (子), with a hand and stick (攵) urging effort — the picture of teaching.
poem: Patterns (爻) shown to a little child (子),
a hand with a stick (攵) keeps lessons mild,
repeat the rule, again, again,
to TEACH (jiāo) a mind and sharpen a pen.

meanings.def: for; to (marks the recipient of an action)

compositionNote: 纟 (thread, originally 'to supply cloth/silk') combines with 合 (hé, to join, also the sound hint) to picture handing something over — to give.
poem: A thread (纟) links two hands as one (合),
合 lends the sound, the deed is done,
pass it over, hand to hand,
to GIVE (gěi) — a gift, freely planned.

compositionNote: 八 (to divide) placed over 厶 (private, personal) pictures setting aside private interest to reach what is shared by all — 'public'.
poem: Split (八) away all private greed (厶),
share it out, that's all we need,
open to all, fair and free,
PUBLIC (gōng) space for you and me.

components.meaning: a container held up (twenty, here a shape)

compositionNote: Originally a picture of two hands (now shaped like 八) lifting an object (廿) together — hence 'shared, together'.
poem: Two hands (八) lift a box (廿) up high,
carrying it together, side by side,
shared the load, shared the fun,
TOGETHER (gòng) — a job that's jointly done.

compositionNote: Water (氵) becoming air (气) pictures water turning into vapor — steam.
poem: Water (氵) turns to rising air (气),
puffing steam without a care,
engines hiss, wheels start to spin,
STEAM (qì) power — let the ride begin.

components.meaning: a bent-over figure with a mouth (口) issuing a command

compositionNote: 司 pictures a figure issuing orders from an open mouth (口) — the root idea of managing or being in charge.
poem: A mouth (口) speaks out, commands take flight,
a bent-over figure, full of might,
orders given, rules in place,
IN CHARGE (sī) — running the whole case.

compositionNote: 辶 (walking) with 斤 (axe) as a sound hint pictures traveling only a short distance — 'near'.
poem: An axe (斤) rings out just down the road,
feet (辶) don't travel far to unload,
just a step, not far to roam,
NEAR (jìn) at hand, so close to home.

compositionNote: In the traditional story behind the glyph, an ox's horns (牛) are tied with wood to warn people, and a mouth (口) below announces the warning — to tell, to announce.
poem: An ox (牛) with horns tied up so tight,
a mouth (口) calls out to warn of the sight,
spread the word, let everyone know,
TELL (gào) them all before you go.

meanings.def: to complain, sue (as in 诉讼)

compositionNote: 讠 (speech) combines with 斥 (chì, to denounce, also a sound hint) — speaking out to relate a story or air a grievance.
poem: Words (讠) spill out, a voice that scolds (斥),
telling a story that unfolds,
pouring the heart out, plain and clear,
TO TELL (sù) — let the whole truth appear.

compositionNote: 哥 stacks 可 twice; originally a phonetic loan character, it settled into meaning 'older brother'.
poem: Two 'ke's (可可) stacked, one on the other,
a title of respect for a brother,
older, wiser, leading the way,
BROTHER (gē) — that's what the elders say.

compositionNote: 口 marks this as a character used mainly for its sound, with 加 (jiā) supplying that sound — borrowed to spell the foreign word 'coffee' in 咖啡.
poem: A mouth (口) sips, wanting more (加) to add,
加 hums the sound, not bitter or bad,
borrowed sounds from a far-off land,
a KA (kā) syllable, coffee in hand.

compositionNote: 口 shows this character is used purely for its sound, with 非 (fēi) supplying that sound — completing the loanword 咖啡 (coffee).
poem: A mouth (口) hums a sound that's not (非) quite plain,
非 lends the note, again and again,
paired with 咖 to brew the day,
FEI (fēi) — the smell of coffee's here to stay.

compositionNote: 子 (child) with 亥 (hài) as a sound hint names a young child.
poem: A little one (子) plays without a care,
亥 hums the sound floating in the air,
giggles and games, small hands, small feet,
a CHILD (hái) — innocent and sweet.

components.meaning: not (borrowed here just for its shape)

compositionNote: 还 simplifies 還 by swapping the original phonetic part for the simpler-looking 不, combined with 辶 (movement) — to return, or (as hái) still going, also.
poem: Not (不) quite done, still on the go (辶),
one more step before you know,
still here, still true, and more also,
STILL (hái) and yet, the story flows.

components.meaning: (gives the sound, from an old place name)

compositionNote: 钅 (metal) with 㕣 (yǎn) as a sound hint names the soft grey metal lead, familiar today from pencil 'lead' (铅笔).
poem: Metal (钅) soft and grey as rain,
㕣 hums a sound to name,
heavy and dull, it leaves a trace,
LEAD (qiān) — in a pencil's writing space.

meanings.def: for sums of money or funds

compositionNote: A bamboo shaft (竹) topped with hair (毛) for the brush tip — the ancient writing brush, now any pen or pencil.
poem: Bamboo (竹) stem meets a tuft of hair (毛),
dipped in ink with writerly care,
strokes and lines, a story told,
the PEN (bǐ) that turns thoughts into gold.

compositionNote: A person (人) standing between two dividing lines (八) pictures being 'in between' — extended to 'introduce', bringing two sides together.
poem: A person (人) stands between two lines (八),
neither here nor there — the borderline,
bringing two sides face to face,
INTRODUCE (jiè) — a bridge, a common space.

compositionNote: 纟 (silk, hinting at connecting threads) sits beside 召 (zhào, summon) as a phonetic hint, together giving the sense of linking people together — to introduce.
poem: A silken thread (纟) heeds the call (召),
stringing new friends, one and all.
To INTRODUCE, to weave the bond —
shào (绍) ties the names beyond.

meanings.def: to be engaged in; to devote effort to

compositionNote: A downward step (夂) presses onto strength (力) below, picturing effort applied to a task — one's business or duty.
poem: A step (夂) comes down upon your strength (力),
pushing duty to full length.
Every TASK you must pursue —
that's wù (务): the business left to do.

meanings.def: member; staff; person engaged in some field

compositionNote: A round mouth (口) sits above a cowrie shell (贝, ancient money), together suggesting one counted and paid — a member of staff.
poem: A mouth (口) that speaks, a shell (贝) that's paid,
together make an employee's trade.
A MEMBER counted, staffed, and true —
that's yuán (员): one of the crew.

compositionNote: A knife (刂) cuts between two pieces of jade (王, 王), dividing precious stone into equal shares — like sorting people into a class or shift.
poem: Jade (王) and jade (王), split by a knife (刂),
divided evenly, sliced just right.
A CLASS, a shift, a working crew —
bān (班) sorts the many into few.

compositionNote: A person (亻) divides up an ox (牛) into separate pieces — the origin of counting individual items.
poem: A person (亻) carves an ox (牛) with care,
splitting it to pieces rare.
Count each ITEM, one by one —
jiàn (件): a piece when work is done.

components.meaning: a hand holding a forked recording tool — an ancient scribe at work

compositionNote: Originally a pictograph of a hand grasping a tool used by officials to record affairs — hence 'matter' or 'affair'.
poem: A scribe's hand grips his tool of state,
recording every AFFAIR and fate.
Big or small, shì (事) means the thing —
the matter that today will bring.

compositionNote: The heart (忄) beats beside 青 (qīng, fresh green), lending its sound while the heart lends the meaning of feeling and emotion.
poem: A heart (忄) grows fresh and green (青) inside,
where every FEELING starts to hide.
Love or mood, whatever springs —
qíng (情) is the heart's true things.

components.meaning: simplified phonetic mark from 昜 (yáng, sun rising)

compositionNote: Ground (土) paired with a simplified sun-rising mark (from 昜) gives an open patch of earth — a field or venue.
poem: Ground (土) so wide beneath the sun,
a FIELD where games and crowds are run.
Market, airport, open land —
chǎng (场) is the space where events stand.

meanings.def: familiar prefix before names or kinship terms

compositionNote: A hill (阝) stands beside 可 (kě), which lends its sound — together forming the friendly prefix 阿 used before names.
poem: Beside a hill (阝), a sound so plain (可),
ā (阿) comes gently, like refrain.
Before a name, it's warm and near —
auntie, granny, brother dear.

meanings.def: aunt (mother's sister); informal term for an older woman

compositionNote: A woman (女) stands next to 夷 (yí), which supplies the sound, giving the word for one's aunt.
poem: A woman (女) paired with a foreign sound (夷),
by mother's side an AUNT is found.
Call her yí (姨) with love so true —
she's family, familiar too.

compositionNote: The mouth (口) opens wide as 阿 (ā) lends its sound — a simple exclamation of surprise or emphasis.
poem: A mouth (口) flies open wide in awe,
echoing sound (阿) without a flaw.
Surprise or stress, it's all the same —
a (啊) ends the sentence, softening the claim.

compositionNote: An arrow (矢), short and swift, sits beside 委 (wěi, drooping) — together picturing something short in stature.
poem: An arrow (矢) short, it droops (委) and bends,
a stature small that low descends.
Not tall at all, just SHORT and neat —
ǎi (矮) describes the folk petite.

compositionNote: A woman (女) sitting safely beneath a roof (宀) — the ancient picture of peace and security.
poem: A woman (女) rests beneath a roof (宀),
sheltered safe, that is the proof.
All is calm, all is SAFE and sound —
ān (安) is peace that home has found.

compositionNote: Fresh green (青) lends its sound while 争 (zhēng, to contend) settles down — once the striving ends, stillness remains.
poem: Fresh green (青) watches strife (争) subside,
the fighting stopped, the noise denied.
QUIET falls like evening's hush —
jìng (静) is calm without the rush.

meanings.def: marks the object moved before the verb (把-construction)
for objects with a handle, or a handful

compositionNote: A hand (扌) clings tightly (巴) to something — the core sense of grasping or holding onto an object.
poem: A hand (扌) that clings (巴) and won't let go,
gripping tight from head to toe.
To HOLD an object, firm and true —
bǎ (把) grabs it, just for you.

meanings.def: to move, to relocate; to carry, to shift

components.meaning: kind, sort; carrying on a boat (phonetic)

compositionNote: A hand (扌) works alongside 般 (bān, once meaning to carry by boat) — hands doing the carrying, now meaning to move things.
poem: A hand (扌) that lifts, a boat's own kind (般),
carries boxes left behind.
To MOVE a home, from here to there —
bān (搬) hauls it everywhere.

meanings.def: to do; to handle; to manage; to set up

components.meaning: two marks, remnants of 辛 (labor) flanking the strength

compositionNote: Strength (力) stands flanked by two marks left over from 辛 (hard labor) on either side — effort applied to get things done.
poem: Strength (力) flanked by marks of labor's trace,
working hard to fill the space.
To GET THINGS DONE, that is the plan —
that's the job of bàn (办), hand in hand.

compositionNote: Water (氵) flows level and fair, and 去 (qù, to go) lends its sound — water's fairness became the symbol for law and method.
poem: Water (氵) flows fair and lets go (去) free,
level for all, like it should be.
A LAW, a method, righteous and fair —
fǎ (法) flows justice everywhere.

compositionNote: Food (饣) is wrapped up (包) inside — the stomach wrapped full of food describes feeling full.
poem: Food (饣) wrapped snug (包) inside your belly,
packed so tight it's rather jelly.
No more room, you're FULL, complete —
bǎo (饱) means you've had your treat.

meanings.def: to hug, to embrace; to hold in arms; to carry

compositionNote: Arms (扌) wrap around (包) something dear — the gesture of hugging or holding close.
poem: Two arms (扌) wrap round (包) like a bow,
holding tight, not letting go.
A warm EMBRACE, a tender squeeze —
bào (抱) hugs you close with ease.

compositionNote: Clothing (衤) covers the skin (皮) — something draped over you, extended to being covered or acted upon by another (passive voice).
poem: Cloth (衤) drapes over skin (皮) at night,
a quilt that holds you snug and tight.
Acted upon, by someone led —
bèi (被) means done to, so it's said.

components.meaning: originally a picture of a nose, now 'self'

compositionNote: 自 was originally a pictograph of a nose (now meaning 'self', since people point to their nose to mean 'me'), combined with 畀 for sound to form 鼻.
poem: 自 once drew a NOSE up front,
before it meant 'myself', the brunt.
Add 畀's sound, the meaning's clear —
bí (鼻) sniffs the air right here.

compositionNote: A cart (车) crosses paths (交) with another — comparing which one moves ahead, giving the meaning of comparison.
poem: A cart (车) crosses paths (交) with a rival cart,
racing close from the very start.
Which one's better? COMPARE the two —
jiào (较) decides what's more, what's true.

compositionNote: Under a roof (宀, echoing 塞 sāi, to fill), valuables (贝) are offered up as prizes — the origin of contests and competitions.
poem: Beneath a roof (宀), the shells (贝) are stacked,
prizes waiting to be racked.
Who wins it all? Who takes the crown? —
sài (赛) is the RACE that brings renown.

components.meaning: a slanting stroke piercing through, marking certainty

compositionNote: A single stroke (丿) pierces straight through the heart (心) shape, marking something fixed and certain — what MUST be.
poem: A stroke (丿) cuts straight into the heart (心),
fixed and certain from the start.
No choice at all, it's set in stone —
bì (必) means MUST, in firmest tone.

compositionNote: Fine hairs (彡) grow from the head (页) — originally drawn as a beard on a face, extended to mean something necessarily present, i.e. 'must'.
poem: Fine hairs (彡) sprout out from the head (页),
a beard that grows where chins have spread.
What NEEDS to be, what MUST occur —
xū (须) is certain, like the fur.

components.meaning: hand, again (simplified from 攴, to strike/act)

compositionNote: Words (top, once 言) meet an acting hand (又, once 攴) — speech plus action stirs things up, causing CHANGE.
poem: Words above (亦) meet a striking hand (又),
stirring plans that once were planned.
Nothing stays the way it's been —
biàn (变) means CHANGE, again and again.

compositionNote: One person stands upright (亻) while another is flipped (匕) — a person transformed into a different posture, the picture of change.
poem: One person stands (亻), one flips around (匕),
upside-down without a sound.
From one shape to another true —
huà (化) means TRANSFORM, something new.

meanings.def: to show; to indicate; to reveal

components.meaning: an altar or offering table, seen from the front

compositionNote: A pictograph of an ancient altar with offerings laid across it — gods 'showed' their will through signs upon it, hence 'to show'.
poem: An altar stands with offerings bare,
signs from heaven shown right there.
To SHOW, reveal, make plain and known —
shì (示) displays what once was shown.

meanings.def: to perform, to act; to develop, to evolve

compositionNote: Water (氵) flows on and on, paired with 寅 (yín) for sound — flowing water suggests a story unfolding, hence to perform or develop.

words.meaning: show; to put on a show

poem: Water (氵) flows where 寅 leads the way,
a story building, scene by day.
On the stage, the tale unfurled —
yǎn (演) PERFORMS it for the world.

components.meaning: ice crystal (two dots, radical form of ice)

compositionNote: Two crystal dots (冫), the sign of frost, cling beside water (水) — water frozen hard into ICE.
poem: Two frosty dots (冫) beside the stream (水),
freezing water like a dream.
Cold and hard, a solid slice —
bīng (冰) is water turned to ICE.

compositionNote: Bamboo (⺮) is woven into a container, and 相 (xiāng) lends its sound — bamboo strips woven together to make a box.
poem: Bamboo strips (⺮) woven side by side (相),
forming walls where things can hide.
A sturdy BOX to pack and store —
xiāng (箱) holds your treasures, and much more.

components.meaning: a young shoot just breaking through the soil

compositionNote: A pictograph of a tender plant shoot just pushing up out of the ground — budding potential, hence 'talent' and 'just now'.
poem: A tender shoot breaks through the ground,
fresh potential, freshly found.
Just now sprouted, TALENT waits —
cái (才) is the gift that germinates.

meanings.def: to take part in; to join; to consult

components.meaning: a person standing with arms spread

compositionNote: A person (大) stands beneath shining stars (厶) with rays of light streaming down (彡) — joining in something bigger than oneself.
poem: A person (大) stands beneath the stars (厶),
rays of light (彡) shine near and far.
JOIN the group, don't stand apart —
cān (参) takes part with willing heart.

compositionNote: Strength (力) is boosted by an encouraging voice (口) — cheering someone on adds to their effort.
poem: Strength (力) gets a shout (口) to cheer it on,
more power added till it's strong.
Stack it up, don't take away —
jiā (加) means ADD, come what may.

compositionNote: Grass (艹) grows up early in the morning (早, phonetic) — the fresh green blades of grass.
poem: Green blades (艹) rise up bright and early (早),
dew-kissed fields all soft and curly.
Underfoot, so green, so GRASSY —
cǎo (草) carpets fields, lush and glassy.

components.meaning: a roof-like covering (originally a reclining body)
cloud (used here as a simplified phonetic, replacing 曾)

compositionNote: A roof-like covering (尸) sits over 云 (cloud, a simplified phonetic hint replacing 曾), picturing things stacked one on top of another.
poem: A roof (尸) sits over a cloud (云) below,
stacked up high, layer by layer they grow.
Floor upon floor, a LAYER (céng) so neat,
each story cloud-topped, complete.

meanings.def: to lack, to be short of

components.meaning: drooping, uneven ears of grain (original picture)

compositionNote: The top depicts drooping, uneven ears of grain (𠂹) over 工 (work), picturing something uneven or lacking — the root sense of 'difference' or 'poor'.

words.meaning: to go on a business trip

poem: Drooping grain (𠂹) sits above hard toil (工),
uneven lengths make the harvest spoil.
Not quite right, a shade too BAD (chà),
close, but missing — small gap, ha!

compositionNote: 走 (to run) combines with 召 (zhào, 'to call' — a phonetic hint) to picture running ahead and calling out, i.e., surpassing others.
poem: Running (走) fast, you call (召) ahead the pack,
leaving rivals lagging back.
Zoom right past, no turning track,
SUPER-fast (chāo) — you won't look back.

components.meaning: cloth (a flag marking a trading spot)

compositionNote: A cloth banner (巾) topped by a mark (亠) originally represented a flag hung to mark a trading place — a market, later extended to mean 'city'.
poem: A cloth flag (巾) waves with a mark (亠) on top,
calling traders to stop and shop.
Stalls line up where the banner flies —
a bustling CITY (shì) meets your eyes.

compositionNote: 衤 (clothing) combines with 寸 (cùn, 'inch' — a phonetic hint) to give 衬, meaning a garment worn underneath or something that sets off another.
poem: Clothes (衤) measured out by an inch (寸) so neat,
worn beneath to make things complete.
A LINING (chèn) hides, but plays its part,
setting off the outer art.

compositionNote: 衤 (clothing) plus 彡 (shān, fine decorative lines — also a phonetic hint) form 衫, a light garment such as a shirt.
poem: Clothes (衤) get fine decorative lines (彡),
patterns dance in soft designs.
Light and airy, worn with charm,
a SHIRT (shān) draped over your arm.

compositionNote: 戈 (a weapon) combines with 丁 (dīng, 'nail' — a phonetic hint) to depict completing a task, giving the meaning 'to become, succeed.'
poem: A nail (丁) driven home by a blade (戈) so bold,
the task is finished, brave and told.
Struggle's done, the goal is won —
BECOME (chéng) complete, the deed is done.

compositionNote: 纟 (silk thread, once a measure of spun work) combines with 责 (zé, 'duty' — a phonetic hint) to mean accomplishment or merit.
poem: Silk thread (纟) spun to measure one's duty (责),
work well done shows in its beauty.
Grades and gains, both hard-earned bits —
ACHIEVEMENT (jì) is what merit permits.

compositionNote: 土 (earth, for building walls) combines with 成 (chéng, 'to complete' — a phonetic hint) to depict a completed earthen wall enclosing a city.
poem: Earth (土) piled high till walls are done (成),
ringing homes beneath the sun.
Gates stand guard, the walls stand tall —
a CITY (chéng) rises, earth and all.

compositionNote: 辶 (movement) combines with 尺 (chǐ, 'ruler/a foot' — a phonetic hint) to suggest slow, measured movement — being late or tardy.
poem: Walking (辶) slow, measured by a ruler's span (尺),
dragging feet as best they can.
Clock ticks on, but you're still behind —
LATE (chí) again, oh never mind.

compositionNote: 阝 (a mound or set of steps) combines with 余 (yú, 'remaining' — a phonetic hint), originally depicting stairs being cleared, giving the sense of 'to remove' or 'except'.
poem: Steps (阝) are swept where extras (余) lay,
clearing the mound, sweeping away.
All but one, set the rest apart —
REMOVE (chú) it all, a clean fresh start.

components.meaning: a phonetic component (also seen in 沿)

compositionNote: 舟 (a boat) combines with 㕣 (a phonetic component seen in characters like 沿) to give 船, meaning boat or ship.
poem: A little boat (舟) sails with sound (㕣) in tow,
gliding where the rivers flow.
Waves may rock but on it speeds —
a SHIP (chuán) that meets the sailor's needs.

compositionNote: The top depicts sprouting plants pushing upward (from ancient 艸/屯), warmed by the 日 (sun) below — the picture of spring growth.
poem: Green sprouts (艹) push up toward the sun (日),
warmth returns, the cold is done.
Buds unfurl, the fields turn bright —
SPRING (chūn) awakens day and night.

compositionNote: 讠 (speech) combines with 司 (sī, 'to manage' — a phonetic hint) to give 词, meaning a word or term used in speech.
poem: Speech (讠) is managed (司) with careful art,
choosing words to play their part.
Sound and meaning, tied as one —
a WORD (cí) is spoken, said, and done.

components.meaning: a bound book of bamboo slips

compositionNote: 册 (a bound book of bamboo slips) rests atop 丌 (a stand or table), depicting an important document held with reverence — a classic text or standard.
poem: A bamboo book (册) set upon a stand (丌),
honored words at your command.
Rules and wisdom, bound and fine —
a CLASSIC (diǎn) text through space and time.

components.meaning: a phonetic component derived from 悤 (cōng, 'hasty, alert')

compositionNote: 耳 (ear) combines with a phonetic component derived from 悤 (cōng, suggesting quick, alert thinking) to give 聪, meaning sharp-eared and clever.
poem: Sharp little ears (耳) that catch each sound,
quick minds (总) with wisdom all around.
Nothing slips by, thoughts run along —
CLEVER (cōng) and bright, keen and strong.

components.meaning: a cliff face (visual origin of the left side)
a hand holding a tool, to strike

compositionNote: The left side pictures rock breaking off a cliff, and 殳 shows a hand striking with a tool — together depicting breaking something into a section or segment.
poem: A cliff face (厂) cracks beneath a striking hand (殳),
broken pieces scattered on the land.
Cut apart, a piece, a part —
each SEGMENT (duàn) marks a brand-new start.

compositionNote: 矢 (an arrow, once used as a short measuring stick) combines with 豆 (dòu, 'bean' — a phonetic hint) to mean short in length.
poem: An arrow (矢) small as a single bean (豆),
measures out what's brief and lean.
Not too long, just a little span —
SHORT (duǎn) and quick, as short as it can.

components.meaning: section (phonetic hint, reused for its sound)

compositionNote: 钅 (metal) combines with 段 (duàn, 'section' — a phonetic hint) to mean forging metal by repeated striking.
poem: Metal (钅) struck in glowing sections (段),
hammered hard by strong hands' actions.
Heat and force make iron strong —
FORGED (duàn) and tempered all day long.

components.meaning: a simplified phonetic component (replacing original 柬)

compositionNote: 火 (fire) combines with 东 (a simplified phonetic component, replacing the original 柬 'to select') to mean refining or smelting with fire.
poem: Fire (火) roars where metals turn (东) to gold,
melting rough into something bold.
Heat refines what's crude and plain —
REFINED (liàn) and pure, through fire's flame.

compositionNote: 饣 (food) combines with 我 (wǒ, 'I' — a phonetic hint) to give 饿, meaning 'I' feel the lack of food — hungry.
poem: Food (饣) is all that 'I' (我) can crave,
my stomach growls, my belly's a cave.
Give me a meal, don't let me wait —
I'm HUNGRY (è), oh please don't be late!

components.meaning: a pictograph of the shape of a human ear

compositionNote: 耳 is a pictograph that traces the outline of a human ear.
poem: A simple shape, curved and small,
the picture of an EAR (ěr), that's all.
Sounds float in through this ancient door,
listening close, forevermore.

meanings.def: for flowers, clouds, and similar clusters

compositionNote: 几 (a curved, drooping shape) sits atop 木 (tree), picturing a flower or fruit hanging from a branch — used as the measure word for flowers and clouds.
poem: A blossom droops (几) atop a tree (木) so tall,
hanging soft before its fall.
Count each bloom, each cloud so fluffy —
one little FLOWER (duǒ), soft and puffy.

meanings.def: hair (read fà, as in 头发)

components.meaning: a simplified character without a clear graphical decomposition (derived from 發/髮)

compositionNote: 发 is a modern simplification of the traditional 發 (to send out) and 髮 (hair); the simplified form no longer shows a clear semantic breakdown.
poem: No picture hides in this modern shape,
just strokes combined to help thoughts escape.
Send it out, let it GROW (fā) and spread,
news and hair both come from here, it's said.

compositionNote: 火 (fire) combines with 尧 (yáo — a phonetic hint, simplified from 堯) to mean to burn, roast, or (of a body) run a fever.
poem: Fire (火) leaps high where 尧 stands proud and tall,
flames lick upward, climbing the wall.
Skin runs hot, cheeks start to glow —
BURNING (shāo) fever, embers aglow.

components.meaning: a pictograph, originally a plow or a square-cornered shape

compositionNote: 方 is a pictograph, originally depicting a plow or a square-cornered shape, later extended to mean direction and method.
poem: Four corners drawn, a shape so square,
pointing the way, near and far.
A method found, a path, a place —
SQUARE (fāng) and steady, marking space.

meanings.def: to let out, dismiss (e.g. from school/work)

components.meaning: a hand holding a stick, action

compositionNote: 方 (direction — a phonetic hint) combines with 攵 (a hand holding a stick, suggesting action) to depict driving something away or setting it free — to release or put.

words.meaning: to finish school for the day

poem: A hand with a stick (攵) points a direction (方),
driving it forth without objection.
Let it go, set it wide and free —
RELEASE (fàng) it now, however it'll be.

components.meaning: a pictograph of the shape of a heart

compositionNote: 心 is a pictograph tracing the outline of a heart.
poem: A shape once drawn from an ancient beat,
the picture of a HEART (xīn), so neat.
Feelings stir where thoughts reside,
mind and spirit, side by side.

components.meaning: an ancient bellows or storehouse shape

compositionNote: The top depicts an ancient bellows or storehouse, and 夂 (footprints, 'to walk slowly') below shows returning to it again and again — giving the sense of repeating or returning.
poem: Back to the storehouse, footsteps (夂) retrace,
walking again to the same old place.
Round and round, the cycle's spun —
REPEAT (fù) it well till the task is done.

components.meaning: a simplified form of 習, an ancient picture of a bird's wing (羽) reduced to a few strokes

compositionNote: 习 is a simplified form of 習, which originally showed 羽 (wings, feathers) over 日 (sun) — a young bird flapping its wings repeatedly to learn to fly, hence 'to practice, study.'
poem: A fledgling flaps its wings toward the sun,
trying again till flight is won.
Practice and drill, day by day —
LEARNING (xí) to soar, come what may.

compositionNote: 阝 (a mound or hill) combines with 付 (fù, 'to hand over' — a phonetic hint) to mean attaching close to something, as if placed alongside a hill.
poem: A little hill (阝) where things are handed (付) near,
close beside, always right here.
Stick it on, don't let it stray —
ATTACHED (fù) close by, come what may.

compositionNote: 讠 (speech) combines with 亥 (hài — a phonetic hint) to give 该, originally meaning 'to state completely,' now used for 'should' or 'ought to.'
poem: Words (讠) declared beneath the sign (亥),
telling you what's right and fine.
Duty calls, don't be slow —
you SHOULD (gāi) do it, here we go.

components.meaning: a hand striking or grasping firmly

compositionNote: 敢 derives from hands grasping firmly (now 攵) combined with 古 (gǔ — a phonetic hint), picturing someone boldly seizing something — hence 'to dare.'
poem: Old hands (古) grip tight, refusing to fear,
holding on firm, courage sincere.
Step up bold, don't hesitate —
DARE (gǎn) to act, don't ever wait.

compositionNote: 咸 (xián — a phonetic hint, meaning 'all') sits above 心 (heart), showing the heart being fully touched or stirred — to feel or be moved.
poem: All (咸) the heart (心) can hold is stirred,
moved by every unspoken word.
Something touches deep within —
to FEEL (gǎn) it all, let it begin.

compositionNote: 冃 (a cap or covering) sits over 目 (eye), picturing something covering the eyes — extended to mean recklessly pushing ahead despite the risk, and also 'to emit' (like steam covering something).
poem: A cap (冃) pulled low above the eye (目),
blinding sight beneath the sky.
Push ahead, though danger's near —
RISK (mào) it all, and show no fear.

compositionNote: 冈 (gāng, 'ridge' — a phonetic hint) combines with 刂 (knife, suggesting hardness) to mean firm and tough, or 'just now' (freshly settled).
poem: A ridge (冈) stands hard against the knife (刂),
tough and firm through all of life.
Only moments since it passed by —
JUST NOW (gāng) it happened, don't ask why.

meanings.def: for long thin objects (e.g. sticks, strands)

compositionNote: 根 pairs the tree radical 木 with the phonetic 艮 (gèn), grounding the meaning of 'root' at the base of a tree.
poem: Deep beneath the tree (木) so tall,
艮 hums a sound, that's all —
reaching down where nutrients dwell,
ROOT (gēn) below, the tree's own well.

compositionNote: A hand (扌) grips firmly onto what one dwells on (居, phonetic), giving 据 the sense of holding evidence — 'according to'.
poem: A hand (扌) holds tight to where you dwell (居),
clutching facts it means to tell —
ACCORDING TO (jù) the proof in hand,
evidence is where you stand.

compositionNote: The foot radical 足 plus the phonetic 艮 (gèn) point to the heel, and by extension, following right behind someone — 'with'.
poem: Your foot (足) treads on, with 艮 in tow,
the heel that follows where you go —
WITH (gēn) a friend, right by your side,
footsteps matching, stride for stride.

compositionNote: 更's strokes stack atop 曰, an old ideogram whose original sense of 'change' has faded, leaving today's meaning of 'even more'.
poem: Stack a line above the say-mouth (曰),
crossed by strokes that seal the vow —
EVEN MORE (gèng) than what you knew,
change piles on, then more anew.

compositionNote: An enclosure (囗) fences in the phonetic 元 (yuán), picturing a walled plot of land — a garden.
poem: A wall (囗) wraps 'round the start of things (元),
where blossoms bloom and songbird sings —
a GARDEN (yuán) fenced from the world outside,
nature's plot, enclosed with pride.

compositionNote: An action (攵, a hand tapping/causing) applied to something ancient (古) — the root cause behind an old event, hence 'reason' and 'therefore'.
poem: Old times (古) get tapped by a hand (攵) that acts,
stirring up the ancient facts —
THEREFORE (gù), a reason comes to light,
a story told from bygone night.

compositionNote: A knife (刂) scrapes near the tongue-shaped phonetic 舌 (shé), giving the sense of scraping — and by extension, wind scraping past.
poem: A knife (刂) glides by a tongue (舌) held still,
scraping close with careful skill —
the wind will BLOW (guā) and scrape the air,
whipping past your tousled hair.

components.meaning: a stylized enclosure with a stroke inside, picturing moving air

compositionNote: 风 is a simplified pictograph-like form whose curved outline and inner stroke suggest air swirling and moving.
poem: A curving shape with air held in,
swirling round beneath the skin —
the WIND (fēng) that blows from far away,
whistling through the night and day.

meanings.def: to look after, take care of

components.meaning: head, page — to turn one's head and look

compositionNote: The head radical 页 (originally 'to turn one's head and look back') combines with a simplified phonetic shape to give 顾 its sense of looking after someone.
poem: A head (页) turns back at a door (户) ajar,
checking loved ones near and far —
to LOOK AFTER (gù) them, come what may,
caring eyes that never stray.

compositionNote: Under a roof (宀), each (各, phonetic) visitor arrives — the picture of a guest received into one's home.
poem: Beneath a roof (宀), each (各) one arrives,
a GUEST (kè) whose visit soon revives —
tea is poured and seats are spread,
welcome words are gently said.

compositionNote: The heart radical 忄 pairs with the phonetic 圣 purely for sound, capturing a feeling too odd to explain — 'strange'.
poem: A heart (忄) feels something hard to say,
a sound (圣) that echoes, come what may —
how STRANGE (guài) this feeling, out of place,
a puzzled look upon your face.

meanings.def: building for public use (hall, hotel, embassy)

compositionNote: Food (饣) served under an official's (官) roof pictures a public hall — a restaurant, library, or embassy.
poem: Food (饣) is served where officials (官) stay,
a grand HALL (guǎn) built to please and sway —
books or noodles, art on view,
a public place for me and you.

meanings.def: to be used to, accustomed to

components.meaning: to pass through, a string of coins (phonetic)

compositionNote: A habit runs through the heart (忄) like coins strung on a cord (贯, phonetic), giving 惯 its sense of being 'used to' something.
poem: Coins (贯) strung through, heart (忄) feels the same,
a threaded string that has no shame —
USED TO (guàn) it now, this well-worn way,
habits strung through every day.

compositionNote: Water (氵) flows alongside the phonetic 可 (kě), forming the character for a flowing river.
poem: Water (氵) flows where it may (可) go,
winding on in gentle flow —
a RIVER (hé) wide, a river deep,
secrets that the currents keep.

compositionNote: Fire (灬) burns beneath a chimney (囱), and the soot it leaves behind gives 黑 its meaning of 'black'.
poem: Fire (灬) burns beneath a smoky flue (囱),
soot collects in shadowed hue —
BLACK (hēi) as night, as coal, as tar,
darkness spreading near and far.

compositionNote: A flat piece of wood (木) turned over (反, phonetic) becomes a board or plank.
poem: Wood (木) flipped over (反), flat and wide,
a sturdy BOARD (bǎn) to write beside —
chalk marks dance across its face,
a plank that holds its steady place.

compositionNote: A hand (扌) bars the door (户, phonetic) shut, the picture of guarding and protecting.
poem: A hand (扌) holds firm against the door (户),
guarding what lies at its core —
PROTECT (hù) the ones you cherish so,
a shield against the wind and woe.

components.meaning: bright, clear (日 sun + 召 to summon, phonetic)

compositionNote: Fire's light (灬) joins 昭 (zhāo, 'bright,' itself sun 日 plus 召), doubling the brightness — to shine or to photograph.
poem: Sun (日) calls out (召), and flames (灬) ignite,
doubling up the beams of light —
SHINE (zhào) a picture, capture the glow,
a flash that freezes time's swift flow.

compositionNote: A plant (艹) transforms (化, phonetic) as it blooms into a flower.
poem: A plant (艹) transforms (化), bud into bloom,
petals bursting, sweet perfume —
a FLOWER (huā) blooms, so bright, so brief,
then money's spent like falling leaf.

components.meaning: field, the framed area being outlined

compositionNote: A line (一) is drawn to frame a field-like area (田), the ancient image of marking out boundaries — 'to draw'.
poem: A line (一) wraps 'round a framed-in field (田),
boundaries where the colors yield —
DRAW (huà) a picture, brush in hand,
a painted world at your command.

compositionNote: Earth (土) that is not (不) sound crumbles apart — the sense of 'bad' or 'broken'.
poem: Earth (土) that's simply not (不) quite right,
crumbles softly out of sight —
BROKEN (huài), BAD, it falls apart,
a cracked foundation from the start.

compositionNote: Jade (王, from 玉) shaped into a circle, with 不 standing in as a simplified phonetic — the picture of a jade ring.
poem: Jade (王) curves 'round in a perfect loop,
a shining RING (huán) in a jeweler's group —
surroundings circle you like this too,
the whole environment wrapping you.

compositionNote: Land (土) reaches its finishing edge (竟, phonetic), marking a border or territory — and by extension, one's surrounding situation.
poem: Land (土) runs out where it must end (竟),
a BORDER (jìng) line the maps append —
beyond this edge, a different place,
a shifting state, a changing space.

meanings.def: to exchange, to change, to switch

compositionNote: A hand (扌) trades one splendid thing (奂, phonetic) for another — to exchange or switch.
poem: A hand (扌) trades something fine and grand (奂),
passing treasure hand to hand —
EXCHANGE (huàn) it now, this thing for that,
swap your coat, your cash, your hat.

components.meaning: a stalk of ripened grain (middle part)
eight, here forming rays at the bottom

compositionNote: 黄 once pictured a person wearing a bright jade pendant; today it reads as ripened grain (由) glowing with rays (八) — the color yellow.
poem: Ripe grain (由) glows, rays (八) spread out wide,
gold light pouring, field-side —
YELLOW (huáng) sun on autumn's crop,
a golden shimmer, never stop.

compositionNote: Bamboo strips (⺮, once used for writing) fit together (合, phonetic) to record a reply — 'to answer'.
poem: Bamboo strips (⺮) fit close and tight (合),
words recorded left to right —
ANSWER (dá) written, question met,
a reply that won't be forgot yet.

compositionNote: 或 once pictured a territory (口 with a boundary) defended by a weapon (戈) — 'a state' — later borrowed for the abstract sense of 'or, perhaps'.
poem: A weapon (戈) guards a walled-in ground (口),
a border kept, a boundary found —
OR (huò) this way, PERHAPS that road,
two choices on the path you strode.

meanings.def: suffix meaning 'one who' or 'the person that' (-er)

compositionNote: 者 is commonly remembered as an elder (耂) speaking through the day (日), marking 'the one who' does or says something.
poem: An elder (耂) speaks throughout the day (日),
the ONE WHO (zhě) has so much to say —
a writer, reader, doer too,
the suffix marking me and you.

compositionNote: Grain (禾) ripening with the youngest child (子) of the harvest gave 季 its meaning of a recurring season.
poem: Grain (禾) ripens where the youngest (子) plays,
cycling through the turning days —
each SEASON (jì) brings a fresh new start,
spring to winter, worlds apart.

compositionNote: Grass/bamboo (艹) above a joint-shaped seal (卩) recalls the segmented nodes of bamboo — a 'joint,' and by extension a festival marking a segment of the year.
poem: Bamboo (艹) bends at a joint (卩) so neat,
segments marking each repeat —
a FESTIVAL (jié) node upon the year,
saving bits to hold them dear.

compositionNote: Words (讠) spoken about oneself (己, phonetic) are set down to be recalled later — 'to remember' or 'to record'.
poem: Words (讠) about yourself (己) take shape,
a memory that won't escape —
REMEMBER (jì) it, write it down,
a diary page, a treasured crown.

compositionNote: A wooden tally (木) checked all together (佥, phonetic) gives 检 its sense of inspection.
poem: A wooden tag (木), checked all as one (佥),
nothing missed before you're done —
INSPECT (jiǎn) it closely, every part,
a careful check from the very start.

meanings.def: to look up (e.g. in a dictionary)

compositionNote: A tree (木) at dawn (旦, phonetic) — originally a tree name, later borrowed for the sense of 'to check' or 'investigate'.

words.meaning: to look up in a dictionary

poem: A tree (木) stands still at break of dawn (旦),
waiting there till night is gone —
CHECK (chá) it closely, page by page,
investigate at every stage.

compositionNote: Bamboo writing slips (⺮) arranged with space between them (间, phonetic) were the earliest 'simple' records — hence 'simple, brief'.
poem: Bamboo slips (⺮) with gaps between (间),
a stripped-down message, spare and clean —
SIMPLE (jiǎn) words on a slender page,
brief and clear from a bygone age.

components.meaning: two dots (top, from a forked tool shape)
ten (stylized shaft of the ancient tool)

compositionNote: 单 originally drew a simple forked hunting tool; its parts no longer carry separate meaning, but together suggest something single and uncombined.
poem: A forked old tool, one shaft alone (十),
two dots (丷) above like seeds once sown —
just SINGLE (dān), simple, one clean part,
no tangled threads, a plain, clear start.

compositionNote: A person (亻) who is well-built (建, phonetic) is strong and healthy.
poem: A person (亻) built (建) up strong and true,
muscles growing, straight of view —
HEALTHY (jiàn) now, robust and spry,
fitness reaching for the sky.

compositionNote: A broad shelter (广) covers grain husks scattering below (隶) — abundant grain safely stored suggests peace and good HEALTH.
poem: A wide roof (广) shelters grain below,
kept safe and dry as seasons go,
well-fed, well-housed, strong and spry —
that's HEALTHY (kāng), standing high!

compositionNote: The speech radical (讠) combines with 井 (jǐng) as a phonetic hint, giving the sound and sense of speaking or explaining.
poem: Words (讠) drop into a deep stone well (井),
echoing out the tales we tell,
open your mouth and let it ring —
that's how to SPEAK (jiǎng): just say the thing!

components.meaning: ancient picture of a curved animal horn

compositionNote: 角 is itself a pictograph — the original drawing of a pointed, ridged animal horn, later extended to mean any pointed corner.
poem: A single picture, sharp and curled,
an animal's horn against the world,
corners poke out, edges appear —
that's a HORN, or corner (jiǎo), here!

components.meaning: to retreat; but (sound hint for jiǎo)

compositionNote: The flesh radical (月) plus 却 (què), used here as a phonetic hint, together point to a part of the body: the foot.
poem: Flesh (月) that won't retreat (却) or flee,
planted firm and steady, see,
down below where two legs connect —
that's the FOOT (jiǎo) you use to trek!

compositionNote: A hand (扌) reaching out, with 妾 (qiè) giving a phonetic hint, gives the sense of receiving or connecting with someone.
poem: A hand (扌) reaches out, warm and true,
greeting guests as they come through,
linking arms, joining a chain —
that's to RECEIVE (jiē), again, again!

compositionNote: Two 'walking' strokes (彳 and 亍, together forming 行) frame 圭 (guī), a phonetic hint, picturing feet moving along a street.

words.meaning: to stroll the streets; go shopping
to go out onto the street

poem: Left foot steps (彳), a jade charm gleams (圭),
right foot follows (亍), or so it seems,
rows of shops where people flow —
that's the STREET (jiē) where crowds all go!

compositionNote: Silk thread (纟) tied around 吉 (jí, 'lucky'), used here as a phonetic hint, gives the idea of tying a knot.
poem: Silk thread (纟) wraps round something lucky (吉),
knotted tight, secure and plucky,
bound together, start to end —
that's how you TIE (jié) a knot, my friend!

components.meaning: ancient picture of a bundle of wood tied round the middle

compositionNote: 束 is an old pictograph showing a bundle of sticks bound tightly at the middle, giving the sense of tying or a bundle.
poem: A bundle of wood, tied round its middle,
sticks held snug, no room to fiddle,
wrapped up tight from end to end —
that's a BUNDLE (shù), a rope its friend!

compositionNote: A knife (刀) cutting an ox's (牛) horn (角) apart pictures the act of dividing something complex — to untie, solve, or explain.
poem: A horn (角), a knife (刀), and an ox (牛) appear,
cutting apart what's tangled here,
slice the knot, make the puzzle clear —
that's to SOLVE (jiě) whatever's near!

components.meaning: to break off; resolute (sound hint for jué)

compositionNote: The ice/water radical (冫) with 夬 (guài), a phonetic hint meaning 'to break off decisively', points to making a firm decision.
poem: Ice (冫) cracks apart, resolute and bold (夬),
the choice is made, the die is told,
no more waiting, no delay —
that's to DECIDE (jué), come what may!

components.meaning: former times; past (sound hint for jiè)

compositionNote: A person (亻) reaching back to the past (昔), used as a phonetic hint, gives the sense of borrowing or lending.
poem: A person (亻) reaches back to olden days (昔),
asking to borrow in so many ways,
lend a book, a cup, a hand —
that's to BORROW (jiè), understand!

components.meaning: village; unit of distance (sound hint for lǐ)

compositionNote: Jade (王) carved along its natural veins, plus 里 (lǐ) as a phonetic hint, gives the sense of pattern, reason, and order.
poem: Jade (王) is carved along its grain,
shaped with logic, not in vain,
ordered like a village clear and neat (里) —
that's the REASON (lǐ) that makes it complete!

meanings.def: long (of time); for a long time

components.meaning: ancient picture of a person being held back or braced, suggesting delay

compositionNote: 久 is an old pictograph of a figure being restrained or braced from behind, drawing out the moment — hence 'a long time'.
poem: A tiny figure, held, delayed,
waiting long while time is stayed,
minutes stretch, the hours accrue —
that's LONG (jiǔ) — it takes a while, it's true!

components.meaning: a simple vertical stroke, like a worn pole

compositionNote: A weathered pole (丨) standing beside the sun (日) that has risen on it day after day suggests something worn with age — OLD.
poem: A pole (丨) beside the sun (日) each day,
weathered, worn, and turning gray,
seen so many suns go by —
that's OLD (jiù): the years pile high!

compositionNote: A mouth (口) wrapped up (勹) into a neat, complete package of words gives the idea of a finished SENTENCE.
poem: Wrapped up (勹) around a mouth (口) so small,
words enclosed, both short and tall,
a thought tied up, complete, construed —
that's a SENTENCE (jù), neatly glued!

meanings.def: to decide; to fix; to set

components.meaning: straight; correct (feet coming to a stop)

compositionNote: Feet coming to a stop (正) under a roof (宀) picture someone settling down — hence 'fixed' or 'certain'.
poem: Under a roof (宀), feet stand firm and true (正),
settled now, with nothing left to do,
the matter's fixed, the plan's in place —
that's DEFINITE (dìng): a settled case!

compositionNote: Water (氵) paired with 曷 (hé), used as a phonetic hint, points to the body craving water — THIRSTY.

words.meaning: to yearn for; to thirst for

poem: Water (氵) longed for, dry throat's plea (曷),
craving a drink so desperately,
parched and dry, wanting more —
that's THIRSTY (kě) down to your core!

meanings.def: a quarter of an hour; a moment

compositionNote: A knife (刂) beside 亥 (hài), used as a phonetic hint, shows the act of cutting marks into something — to CARVE.
poem: A knife (刂) cuts marks by an ancient sign (亥),
carving lines in careful design,
each little notch, a moment's trace —
that's to CARVE (kè), or a MOMENT's space!

compositionNote: A hollow cave (穴) dug by hard work (工), used here as a phonetic hint, gives the idea of empty space.
poem: A cave (穴) dug out by careful work (工),
hollow inside, where shadows lurk,
nothing left but air and space —
that's EMPTY (kōng), an open place!

meanings.def: to adjust; to mix; to blend

compositionNote: Speech (讠) combined with 周 (zhōu, 'cycle'), used as a phonetic hint, points to adjusting or tuning something until it's right.
poem: Words (讠) go round in weekly cycles (周),
tuning, mixing, working through you,
adjust the settings, get it right —
that's to ADJUST (tiáo) both day and night!

meanings.def: for family members; for things with an opening

components.meaning: ancient picture of an open mouth

compositionNote: 口 is itself a pictograph of a simple open mouth, shown as a square opening.
poem: A simple square, open and wide,
a picture of a mouth, open-eyed,
words come out and food goes in —
that's the MOUTH (kǒu) where sounds begin!

compositionNote: Two mouths (口口) wailing above a dog (犬) picture loud, uncontrolled howling — to CRY.
poem: Two mouths (口口) wail like a dog's (犬) sad cry,
howling loud beneath the sky,
tears fall down, the sobs pour through —
that's to CRY (kū), boo-hoo-hoo!

compositionNote: The clothing radical (衤) with 库 (kù, 'warehouse') as an exact phonetic match gives both sound and sense: clothing for the legs.
poem: Clothing (衤) stored inside a warehouse (库),
folded pants, both new and old,
two legs slide in, side by side —
that's your PANTS (kù) you wear with pride!

compositionNote: Bamboo (竹) paired with 快 (kuài, 'fast'), an exact phonetic match, names the quick bamboo sticks used for eating.
poem: Bamboo (竹) sticks, quick (快) and light,
picking up your food just right,
two thin sticks that work as one —
CHOPSTICKS (kuài) make the eating fun!

compositionNote: The grass radical (艹), for the indigo plant once used to make dye, combines with 监 (jiān) as a phonetic hint to give BLUE.
poem: A plant (艹) once watched with careful eye (监),
dyed indigo beneath the sky,
color of the sea and air —
that's the color BLUE (lán) laid bare!

components.meaning: ancient picture of a tiger, showing its head, stripes, and legs

compositionNote: 虎 is an old pictograph drawn to resemble a standing tiger with its open mouth and striped body.
poem: Stripes and claws in ancient guise,
a fearsome shape before your eyes,
king of the jungle, bold and true —
that's the TIGER (hǔ) stalking you!

components.meaning: a simplified curling stroke standing in for the original phonetic 豊

compositionNote: The altar radical (礻), for ritual and worship, combines with a simplified stroke (乚) replacing the old phonetic 豊, giving CEREMONY.
poem: An altar (礻) bows with a curling line (乚),
offerings placed, a sacred sign,
manners shown and gifts bestowed —
that's the CEREMONY (lǐ) that's owed!

components.meaning: do not (exact sound match for wù)

compositionNote: An ox (牛) beside 勿 (wù, 'do not'), an exact phonetic match, broadened over time to mean any THING or object.
poem: An ox (牛) warned back by a do-not sign (勿),
yet still it works the whole day's time,
creatures, goods, and things at hand —
that's a THING (wù) across the land!

compositionNote: Under a cliff (厂), strength (力) is exerted step by step through time — giving the sense of passing through, or HISTORY.
poem: Under a cliff (厂), with strength (力) to spare,
trudging through the years, everywhere,
seasons passed and days gone by —
that's HISTORY (lì) reaching high!

components.meaning: ancient picture of a hand holding a recording tool, like a scribe keeping records

compositionNote: 史 pictures a hand grasping a document or brush — the ancient scribe who recorded events, giving us HISTORY.
poem: A steady hand holds a scribe's own tool,
recording facts by an ancient rule,
writing down what's come to pass —
that's HISTORY (shǐ), built to last!

compositionNote: The flesh radical (月) with 佥 (qiān), used as a phonetic hint, points to the fleshy part where all your features meet — the FACE.
poem: Flesh (月) shaped smooth, all brought together (佥),
features formed to last forever,
eyes and nose and mouth in place —
that's your FACE (liǎn), your own true face!

meanings.def: to practice; to train; to drill

components.meaning: east (simplified stand-in for the original phonetic 柬)

compositionNote: Thread (纟) that must be worked and pulled repeatedly, with 东 replacing the old phonetic 柬, gives the sense of PRACTICE.
poem: Thread (纟) pulled taut, looped and refined (东),
worked again till it's aligned,
drill it daily, don't give in —
that's to PRACTICE (liàn) till you win!

compositionNote: The vehicle radical (车) with 两 (liǎng, 'two'), a close phonetic hint, gives the measure word used for counting vehicles.
poem: A cart (车) counted, one then two (两),
lined up waiting in a queue,
count them all along the road —
that's the word for CARS (liàng), each load!

compositionNote: An ear (耳) leaning in, with 卯 (mǎo) as a phonetic hint, points to listening closely while chatting.
poem: An ear (耳) leans in at a certain call (卯),
listening close to hear it all,
words flow easy, back and forth —
that's to CHAT (liáo), south and north!

components.meaning: order; command (close sound hint for lín)

compositionNote: 令 (lìng), a close phonetic hint, combines with the settlement radical (阝) to mean someone living in the same settlement — NEIGHBOR.
poem: An order given (令) near your place (阝),
living close, right by your space,
just next door, not far to roam —
that's your NEIGHBOR (lín), near your home!

meanings.def: to reside; to live (in a place)

components.meaning: a reclining person; body (suggests a dwelling)

compositionNote: A reclining figure (尸), suggesting someone settled at home, combines with 古 (gǔ) as a phonetic hint to mean RESIDE.
poem: A reclining form (尸) from days of old (古),
settled down as the story's told,
making a home, staying put —
that's to RESIDE (jū), putting down foot!

compositionNote: 木 (wood, the building material) is paired with 娄, which lends its sound lóu, giving a tall wooden structure built floor upon floor.
poem: A tree (木) grows tall, floor after floor,
娄 lends its sound, and even more —
Room upon room, a BUILDING (lóu) so grand,
Reaching high above the land!

components.meaning: phonetic, gives a sound close to lǜ; also means 'to record'

compositionNote: 纟 (silk) shows the color came from dyeing thread, while 录 supplies the lǜ sound.
poem: Silk threads (纟) dyed in leafy hue,
录 lends its sound, and colors true —
Grass and leaves in springtime dressed,
GREEN (lǜ) is nature at its best!
