components.meaning: a horse, seen from the side, with mane and legs

compositionNote: 马 is a simplified pictograph of a horse's head, mane, and legs, reduced from the more detailed traditional 馬.
poem: Four legs, a mane that flows and flies,
A HORSE (mǎ) gallops 'neath the skies —
One simple shape, both swift and free,
Racing wild across the lea!

meanings.def: to fill; to reach the limit of

components.meaning: altered from 㒼, a phonetic element giving the mǎn sound

compositionNote: 氵 (water) shows liquid rising toward the brim, while the right side (derived from 㒼) gives the mǎn sound.
poem: Water (氵) rises to the brim,
两-shaped walls can't hold it in —
Cup and heart alike overflow,
FULL (mǎn) is all that they can show!

components.meaning: phonetic, also means 'to emit, to risk'

compositionNote: 巾 (cloth) is the material, while 冒 gives both the mào sound and a hint of something popping out over the head.
poem: Cloth (巾) wrapped 'round to brave the cold,
冒 pokes out, both sound and bold —
Perched up top from morn to night,
A HAT (mào) that keeps your head just right!

compositionNote: 合 (bring together) sits above 手 (hand), showing a hand closing around something to take hold of it.
poem: Bring things together (合), that's the plan,
Then use a hand (手) to hold what you can —
Grip it, grab it, hold it tight,
TO TAKE (ná) it firmly, day or night!

compositionNote: 入 (enter) is shown moving inside 冂 (an enclosure), giving the idea of the space within.
poem: A boundary box (冂) stands on guard,
入 slips in, past the yard —
Step across, and you will find
INSIDE (nèi), the world confined!

components.meaning: a bird, showing its head, wing, and tail

compositionNote: 鸟 is a simplified pictograph tracing the outline of a bird's head, body, wing, and tail.
poem: A head, a wing, a tail that's small,
This little shape says it all —
Perched and chirping, watch it soar,
A BIRD (niǎo) that sings forevermore!

components.meaning: phonetic, gives a sound close to nǔ; also means 'slave'

compositionNote: 力 (strength) is added beneath 奴, which supplies the nǔ sound, showing strength being pushed to its limit.

words.meaning: to pout one's lips (as a signal)

poem: Once a servant (奴), bound by chains,
Now pours strength (力) through aching veins —
Push and sweat, don't ever stop,
STRIVE (nǔ) your hardest to the top!

components.meaning: a flexed arm muscle or a plow, symbolizing physical strength

compositionNote: 力 is a pictograph of a strong, flexed arm (or a plow handle), representing muscular effort and power.
poem: A flexed arm, a farmer's plow,
Muscle straining here and now —
Push and pull with all you've got,
That's raw POWER (lì), give it your shot!

components.meaning: phonetic, gives the sound bā, close to pá

compositionNote: 爪 (a claw-like hand) shows the grabbing motion of climbing, while 巴 supplies the pá sound.
poem: Claws (爪) dig in, up the wall you scale,
巴 hangs on, don't ever fail —
Hand by hand and knee by knee,
CLIMB (pá) as high as high can be!

meanings.def: for coiled or plate-shaped things, or a game (e.g. of chess)

components.meaning: boat-like top, a remnant of 般 (to carry)

compositionNote: 皿 (a vessel) forms the base, while the boat-like top comes from 般 (to carry), showing something carried on a wide dish.
poem: A boat-like top glides on with grace,
皿 the dish holds food in place —
Round and flat, it serves with pride,
A TRAY (pán) with dinner set inside!

components.meaning: phonetic, gives the sound bàn, close to pàng

compositionNote: 月 (flesh) shows this relates to the body, while 半 gives a sound close to pàng.
poem: Half (半) a body (月) grown so round,
Extra pounds from feasts abound —
Jolly belly, cheeks that glow,
Simply FAT (pàng) from head to toe!

components.meaning: a hand pulling hide or skin off an animal

compositionNote: 皮 is a pictograph of a hand stripping the hide from an animal, giving the meaning of skin or leather.
poem: A hand reaches out to peel and pull,
Stripping hide till the bag is full —
Tough and thin, it wraps us tight,
SKIN (pí) that's covering day and night!

components.meaning: phonetic, gives a sound close to xié

compositionNote: 革 (leather) is the material, while 圭 lends its sound to complete xié.
poem: Leather (革) cut and stitched with care,
圭 lends the sound that shoes will wear —
Slip them on before you dash,
A SHOE (xié) to walk with style and flash!

meanings.def: used only in 啤酒 (beer); a phonetic transliteration character

components.meaning: phonetic, gives a sound close to pí

compositionNote: 口 (mouth) hints at drinking, while 卑 was chosen purely for its sound to transliterate the foreign word 'beer'.
poem: A mouth (口) that drinks, a borrowed sound (卑),
A fizzy word for bubbly brew —
Clink your glass and take a sip,
BEER (pí) makes every party zip!

compositionNote: 氵 (liquid) is added to 酉, a pictograph of a wine jar, together showing fermented drink.
poem: Water (氵) poured in a clay jar (酉) deep,
Fermenting secrets it will keep —
Raise a glass and toast tonight,
WINE (jiǔ) that makes the mood so light!

components.meaning: together, side by side; phonetic hint

compositionNote: 瓦 (earthenware) shows the material, while 并 gives a sound close to píng and suggests pieces joined together to form a vessel.
poem: Clay (瓦) shaped and fired side by side (并),
A vessel standing tall with pride —
Fill it up with drink so cold,
A BOTTLE (píng) for stories told!

components.meaning: a woven winnowing basket, seen from above (original pictograph)

compositionNote: 其 began as a picture of a woven winnowing basket (now written 箕); the shape was borrowed for the grammatical word meaning 'his/its'.
poem: A woven basket, seen from above,
Once held grain, now means 'thereof' —
Borrowed sound for words so small,
HIS/ITS (qí) points to one and all!

components.meaning: simplified shape standing in for 贯, a string of treasure

compositionNote: 宀 (roof) covers a house that once held 贯 (strings of treasure), simplified to a 头-like shape, giving the sense of solid, real wealth inside.
poem: Under a roof (宀), treasures pile in,
A house of wealth, solid within —
No fakes or tricks, just honest ground,
REAL (shí) and true is what is found!

components.meaning: phonetic, gives a sound close to qí

compositionNote: 大 (big, unusual) combines with 可, which lends its sound to complete qí.
poem: Something big (大) that's hard to place,
可 hums its sound with a curious face —
Unusual, weird, off the norm,
STRANGE (qí) things come in every form!

compositionNote: 马 (horse) is the semantic clue for riding, while 奇 supplies the qí sound.
poem: Hop on a horse (马), so strange (奇) and grand,
Reins in hand, you rule the land —
Gallop off through wind and rain,
TO RIDE (qí) is freedom, loose the rein!

compositionNote: 氵 (water) plus 青 (blue-green, pure) shows water so pure it looks blue-green, and 青 also gives the qīng sound.
poem: Water (氵) pure as green-blue skies (青),
Nothing murky meets the eyes —
See right through to pebbles below,
CLEAR (qīng) as streams that gently flow!

meanings.def: clear, neat, distinct (as in 清楚)

compositionNote: 林 (a forest, originally thorny bushes) sits above 疋 (a foot), suggesting pushing through brush to make things clear.
poem: Two trees (林) stand thick, a thorny run,
Feet (疋) push through till the path is done —
Push aside the tangled haze,
See things CLEARLY (chǔ) through the maze!

compositionNote: 禾 (grain) beside 火 (fire) recalls harvest time, when ripened grain glows gold and fields are cleared by burning.
poem: Grain (禾) stands gold in fields of fire (火),
Harvest season, hearts inspire —
Leaves turn red, the air grows cool,
AUTUMN (qiū) breaks the summer's rule!

compositionNote: 衤 (clothing) shows this is a garment, while 君 gives a sound close to qún.
poem: Cloth (衤) fit for a noble lord (君),
Flowing fabric, fashion's reward —
Twirl around from waist to knee,
A SKIRT (qún) that dances gracefully!

components.meaning: phonetic, gives a sound close to rèn

compositionNote: 讠 (speech) shows this relates to saying or naming, while 人 lends a sound close to rèn.
poem: Words (讠) spoken to name a person (人) true,
Calling out 'I know it's you!' —
Faces, facts, and truths made plain,
RECOGNIZE (rèn) again, again!

components.meaning: crossed strokes representing the ribs and handle

compositionNote: 伞 is a pictograph: the 人-shaped top is the canopy, and the crossed strokes below are the ribs and handle of an open umbrella.
poem: A canopy (人) spread wide and round,
Crossed ribs (十) that hold their ground —
Pop it open, rain won't win,
UMBRELLA (sǎn) keeps you dry within!

compositionNote: 扌 (hand) plus a simplified broom shape (from 帚) together show a hand sweeping with a broom.
poem: A hand (扌) grips tight a broom (彐) of straw,
Sweeping dust from every floor —
Back and forth, the mess must go,
SWEEP (sǎo) it clean, row by row!

compositionNote: 口 (mouth) shows this relates to speaking or making sound, while 桑 gives a sound close to sǎng.
poem: A mouth (口) rings out by the mulberry tree (桑),
Singing loud for all to see —
Deep inside where sound is born,
THROAT (sǎng) belts a voice reborn!

meanings.def: for sounds or utterances, e.g. 一声

components.meaning: remnant shape kept from the original stone-chime pictograph
remnant shape from the original character

compositionNote: 声 is a simplified remnant of 聲, which showed a stone chime being heard by an ear (耳); the ear was dropped, leaving only the top shape to mean 'sound'.
poem: A stone chime once rang, an ear would hear,
Now just the chime shape stays right here —
Loud or soft, a ringing tone,
SOUND (shēng) travels far from home!

components.meaning: three 十 (ten) shapes joined together, representing thirty years

compositionNote: 世 originally joined three 十 (ten) shapes to represent thirty years, one generation, later extended to mean 'world' or 'era'.
poem: Three tens joined as one great sign,
Thirty years where lives entwine —
Era, age, and all who dwell,
The WORLD (shì) has quite a tale to tell!

compositionNote: 田 (a field marked with lines) is joined with 介 (between), showing a line dividing two pieces of land.
poem: A field (田) is split by lines (介) so neat,
Marking where two lands will meet —
Border, realm, and world's own place,
BOUNDARY (jiè) defines the space!

compositionNote: 疒 (sickness) frames 叟 (an old man), suggesting someone frail and thin as if bedridden.
poem: Sickness bed where an old man (叟) lies,
Frail and slight before our eyes —
Bones show through with little weight,
THIN (shòu) and slender, small in state!

meanings.def: polite term for a man of one's father's generation

components.meaning: beans on a stalk (a pictograph, also the phonetic)

compositionNote: 叔 combines 尗 (beans on a stalk, also giving the shū sound) with 又 (a hand), originally showing a hand picking beans, later borrowed to mean a father's younger brother.
poem: A hand (又) reaches for beans (尗) on a vine,
Picking gently, one by one, so fine —
Father's brother, kind and true,
UNCLE (shū) shares a joke with you!

meanings.def: to stretch, to unfold, to relax

compositionNote: 舍 (a house, and a hint of the shū sound) pairs with 予 (to give), suggesting a home that gives ease and comfort.
poem: A cozy house (舍) that gives (予) with grace,
Warmth and ease fill up the place —
Stretch out, relax, let worries go,
COMFY (shū) feelings start to flow!

components.meaning: correct, pair — here a graphic simplification of the phonetic 尌

compositionNote: 木 (tree) gives the meaning, while the 对-shaped component is a simplified stand-in for the original phonetic 尌, hinting at the shù sound.
poem: Wood (木) grows tall with branches spread,
对's shape hints the sound instead,
Leaves and roots from earth to sky,
TREE (shù) stands strong as years go by.

components.meaning: a hand holding a stick, action

compositionNote: 攵 (a hand with a stick, action) shows the tallying, while 娄 lends its sound to shù.
poem: A hand with a stick goes tap, tap, tap (攵),
娄 lends a sound, then folds it back,
Counting beads upon a frame,
NUMBER (shù) is the counting game.

compositionNote: Two 又 (hand) shapes side by side simply picture a pair, two of a kind.
poem: Two hands (又又) stand side by side,
A matching set, they won't divide,
Shoes or chopsticks, hand in hand,
PAIR (shuāng) means two, a matching band.

components.meaning: eight — here two even strokes branching apart

compositionNote: 干 (a pole) sits level with two even strokes (八) branching off it, like a balanced scale beam.
poem: A pole (干) stands straight, then splits in two (八),
Even both sides, balanced and true,
No bumps, no tilt, just calm and clean,
FLAT and level (píng) — smooth serene.

meanings.def: yang (the positive principle, opposite of yin)

compositionNote: 阝(a hill/mound) faces 日 (the sun), depicting the sunny, bright side of the hill — yáng.
poem: A hill (阝) turns to greet the sun (日) above,
Bright and warm, the light they love,
Sunny side where shadows fade,
YANG (yáng) is light, not the shade.

compositionNote: 米 (rice/grain) shows its food origin, while 唐 lends the sound táng.
poem: Grains of rice (米) turned sweet and fine,
唐 sings out the sound in line,
Melt it slow, a sugary treat,
SUGAR (táng) makes candy sweet.

compositionNote: 牛 (an ox, once a special sacrificial animal) pairs with 寺 as a sound hint for tè.
poem: An ox (牛) once chosen, set apart,
寺 hums the sound right from the start,
Not common, not the usual bunch,
SPECIAL (tè) stands out from the punch.

components.meaning: sickness radical, a person lying on a sickbed

compositionNote: 疒 (the sickness radical, like a person lying on a sickbed) shows pain, with 冬 giving a sound hint.
poem: Lying sick upon a bed (疒) so cold,
冬's chill gives the sound, we're told,
A throb, an ache, from head to toe,
It HURTS (téng) — but love can grow too.

compositionNote: 扌(a hand) does the lifting and carrying, while 是 lends its sound to tí.
poem: A hand (扌) reaches for the bag's tight rim,
是 hums a sound, though sense grows dim,
Lift it high, then speak your mind,
To RAISE (tí) and mention — both combined.

components.meaning: a man (appears twice, side by side)

compositionNote: Two 夫 (men) stand atop 日 (the sun/day), picturing one person stepping in for another as the day goes by.
poem: Two men (夫夫) stand where the sun (日) shines through,
One steps out, in comes the new,
Taking turns, from me to you,
REPLACE (tì) is what we do.

compositionNote: 舌 (the tongue) tastes 甘 (something sweet) — together, sweetness on the tongue.
poem: The tongue (舌) reaches out to taste what's sweet (甘),
Sugar and honey, a lovely treat,
Smile so bright, a sugary song,
SWEET (tián) is where the tongue belongs.

components.meaning: a simplified, cursive reshaping of the traditional 頭, a picture of a head

compositionNote: 头 is a simplified, cursive reshaping of the traditional 頭, itself a picture of a head.
poem: Once a full head, drawn with care,
Now simplified — swirls of hair,
Sitting high on shoulders, proud,
HEAD (tóu) held up above the crowd.

compositionNote: 犬 (a dog) bursts out from 穴 (a cave/den) — the picture of something sudden and unexpected.
poem: A dog (犬) leaps out from a cave (穴) so tight,
No warning given, pure surprise and fright,
Quick as a flash, it breaks the hush,
SUDDEN (tū) — a startling rush.

components.meaning: winter-shaped simplification of the original inner plan graphic

compositionNote: 囗 (an enclosure) frames the inner part, like a border drawn around a plan or map.
poem: A border (囗) wraps a plan drawn tight,
Winter's shape (冬) peeks out just right,
Roads and rivers, borders too,
A MAP (tú) or picture comes into view.

compositionNote: 月 (flesh/body) shows this is a body part, while 退 lends its sound tuì → tuǐ.
poem: Flesh and bone (月) that help you stand,
退 gives the sound, close at hand,
Walking, running, day by day,
Your LEG (tuǐ) carries you away.

compositionNote: 石 (stone/ceramic material) shows what it's made of, while 宛 gives the exact sound wǎn.
poem: Made of stone or clay (石), so round,
宛 lends the very sound we've found,
Filled with rice or steaming soup,
A BOWL (wǎn) for the family group.

components.meaning: a simplified cursive shape standing in for the complex 萬, originally a picture of a scorpion

compositionNote: 万 is a simplified cursive stroke-shape that replaces the complex traditional 萬 (a picture of a scorpion), now just meaning a huge number.
poem: A scorpion's shape once curled and small,
Now just three strokes, that says it all,
Ten thousand things, a myriad band,
COUNTLESS (wàn) as the grains of sand.

compositionNote: 亻(a person) stands (立) in their place — the idea of a position or a polite way to count people.
poem: A person (亻) stands up straight and tall (立),
In their own spot, they will not fall,
A seat, a rank, a place to be,
POSITION (wèi) — count one, two, three.

compositionNote: 耳 (an ear) presses close to 门 (a door), listening in — originally 'to hear', later also 'to smell'.
poem: An ear (耳) pressed close against the door (门),
Listening hard to hear some more,
A whiff, a scent, drifts through the air,
To SMELL or hear (wén) news everywhere.

components.meaning: deficient, at a loss — phonetic component

compositionNote: 氵(water) turns bad with 亏 (deficient, lacking) beside it — water that has gone dirty or foul.
poem: Water (氵) once clear, now running low (亏),
Murky, muddy, sluggish flow,
Trash and grime beneath the moon,
DIRTY (wū) water, fouled too soon.

meanings.def: to infect; to catch (a habit or disease)

components.meaning: tree, the source of plant dye

compositionNote: Cloth is dipped in 氵(water) with dye from 木 (wood/plants), done 九 (nine, i.e. many) times to make the color take.
poem: Dip it in water (氵) again and again (九),
Dye from the wood (木), a colorful stain,
Nine times over till the shade is true,
DYE (rǎn) it red, or gold, or blue.

meanings.def: to not have; to be without

components.meaning: a simplified skeleton form standing in for the complex 無 (without)

compositionNote: 无 is a streamlined simplification of the complex traditional 無, keeping only a bare skeleton of strokes to mean 'without'.
poem: Complex strokes once danced and twirled,
Now stripped bare, simplest in the world,
Empty-handed, nothing to show,
WITHOUT (wú) means letting go.

compositionNote: 目 (an eye) looks closely at 木 (a tree) — observing closely, a meaning that extended to 'mutual' and 'appearance'.
poem: An eye (目) looks hard at a tree (木) so tall,
Watching closely, taking it all,
Face to face, side by side we stand,
MUTUALLY (xiāng) we lend a hand.

compositionNote: 亻(a person) stands beside 言 (their words) — a person whose words can be trusted.
poem: A person's (亻) word (言) is an honest bond,
Trust is built, of that we're fond,
Sealed in envelopes, sent with care,
BELIEVE (xìn) the letters that we share.

compositionNote: 禾 (ripening grain) sits over what was originally 甘 (sweet), now shaped like 日 — the sweet aroma of grain, fragrant.
poem: Grain (禾) ripens sweet beneath the sun (日),
A lovely scent has just begun,
Bread and rice, a warm bouquet,
FRAGRANT (xiāng) drifting far away.

compositionNote: 艹(the grass/plant radical) shows this is a plant, while 焦 gives the exact sound jiāo.
poem: A leafy plant (艹) beneath the sun,
焦's burnt sound, though not undone,
Yellow peel and sweet inside,
BANANA's (jiāo) treat we can't hide.

compositionNote: 亻(a person) stands beside 象 (elephant, giving both the sound xiàng and the idea of 'form/appearance').
poem: A person (亻) stands by an elephant's (象) shape,
Looking alike, no need to escape,
A mirror image, statue too,
RESEMBLE (xiàng) — it looks like you.

compositionNote: 走 (to run/walk toward something) pairs with 取 (to take), giving the sound qù and the idea of pursuing what interests you.
poem: Running fast (走), reaching to take (取) what's fun,
Chasing joy till the day is done,
Games and laughter, hobbies too,
FUN (qù) and interest — through and through.

meanings.def: to walk; to go; to travel

components.meaning: a picture of a crossroads, where roads meet and people walk

compositionNote: 行 is a pictograph of a crossroads where paths cross — the place where people walk, travel, and do business.
poem: Roads that cross (行), a busy street,
Walkers pass with hurried feet,
"Sure, OK!" — it all works out,
To GO (xíng) or walk, without a doubt.

compositionNote: 木 (a tree) grows 子 (fruit/seeds) — the plum tree, and also a common Chinese surname.
poem: A tree (木) that bears its fruit (子) with pride,
Sweet plums hanging side by side,
A common name passed down with glee,
Mr. LI (lǐ) picks plums from the tree.

components.meaning: able — originally a picture of a bear, later borrowed for 'able'; phonetic component
fire dots, here suggesting the animal's legs

compositionNote: 能 (originally a picture of a bear, later borrowed for 'able') gives the sound, with 灬 added below.
poem: A bear (能), so strong, so able and grand,
Four little legs (灬) help it stand,
Honey and fish, a furry snack,
BEAR (xióng) with a hump upon its back.

compositionNote: 辶(movement) combines with 先 (first) — moving to pick out the one that comes first, i.e., to choose.
poem: Walking forward (辶), picking who goes first (先),
Weighing choices, best or worst,
One stands out among the rest,
CHOOSE (xuǎn) and pick the very best.

compositionNote: 雨 (rain) falls while 而 (a figure waiting) stands below — waiting for what is needed, like farmers needing rain.
poem: Rain (雨) falls down while farmers wait (而),
Praying for it, hoping for fate,
Water for crops, a crucial cue,
What we NEED (xū), we must pursue.

components.meaning: two — here a mark for the top, the head

compositionNote: 二 (a mark for the top/head) sits above 儿 (a person's legs) — a person's head emphasized, meaning 'the beginning, the first'.
poem: A person's (儿) head marked high (二) and clear,
The first, the start, the origin here,
Coins that jingle, money to spend,
One YUAN (yuán) begins, and one will end.

compositionNote: 心 (the heart) sits beneath 原 (which gives the sound yuàn) — a heartfelt wish.
poem: The heart (心) beneath, sincere and true,
原 lends its sound to what we say,
A hope, a dream, a wish held tight,
WILLING (yuàn) hearts make wrongs give way.

meanings.def: (in 越...越..., the more... the more...)

compositionNote: 走 (running/moving) combines with 戉 (an axe shape giving the sound yuè) — to leap over and exceed.
poem: Running fast (走), leaping the wall,
戉's an axe, that's not all,
Further, higher, more each day,
EXCEED (yuè) and race away.

components.meaning: an ancient picture of swirling, rising vapor

compositionNote: 云 is itself an ancient pictograph showing wisps of cloud curling upward, too simple to be split into further parts.
poem: Swirling wisps with no thread spun,
drifting lazy past the sun,
puffy shapes that float and roam —
that's a CLOUD (yún), the sky's own foam.

meanings.def: for flat objects: paper, tickets, tables

components.meaning: long; also a phonetic hint for the sound zhāng

compositionNote: A bow (弓) drawn out long (长) shows a bowstring being stretched wide open, giving both the meaning 'to open' and the sound zhāng.
poem: A bow (弓) drawn long (长), string pulled tight,
it opens wide with all its might,
then counts a sheet, thin and neat —
to OPEN wide is zhāng (张), complete.

meanings.def: again, once more (read chóng, as in 重复)

components.meaning: village; also a unit of distance (Chinese mile)

compositionNote: Picture a thousand (千) miles (里) of road piled onto your shoulders — that crushing load is what makes something 重, 'heavy'.
poem: A thousand (千) miles (里) upon your back,
weigh you down along the track,
such a load makes shoulders bend —
that's HEAVY (zhòng), a weight without end.

components.meaning: a picture of a flame burning steadily atop a lampstand

compositionNote: 主 originally drew a lamp flame fixed on its stand — the steady flame that a household's master keeps tending, hence 'main' and 'host'.
poem: A flame (主) atop its steady stand,
burns bright to light the master's hand,
the one who tends it rules the room —
the MAIN one, zhǔ (主), dispels the gloom.

components.meaning: master, main; also a phonetic hint for zhù

compositionNote: Water (氵) poured exactly where the master (主) points gives 注 its sense of 'pouring' and, by extension, 'focusing attention'.
poem: Water (氵) poured where the master (主) points,
focus flows and never disjoints,
pour your mind where eyes are true —
PAY ATTENTION, that is zhù (注).

components.meaning: a picture of a human nose

compositionNote: 自 was originally a drawing of a nose — ancient Chinese speakers pointed at their nose to mean 'me', so the nose came to mean 'self'.
poem: A nose (自) drawn plain, a pointing sign,
for 'me' the Chinese touch this line,
when speaking of your very own —
that's SELF (zì), the nose you call your throne.

components.meaning: originally a picture of a coiled cord or thread

compositionNote: 己 first drew a bent, coiled cord; the shape was later borrowed purely for its sound to mean 'oneself'.
poem: A coiled thread (己), twisted small,
lent its shape to 'self' for all,
look inward, find your own true face —
that's jǐ (己), SELF in every place.

meanings.def: general, overall, chief (as in 总经理)

components.meaning: a pair of dividing strokes, suggesting many separate things

compositionNote: 总 simplifies the traditional 總 (silk 糸 plus the phonetic 悤); the surviving 心 (heart) at the base suggests many separate thoughts (丷) gathered into one overall whole.
poem: Split thoughts (丷) gathered to the heart (心),
summed up whole, no loose part,
add them ALWAYS, every one —
that's the meaning, zǒng (总), all as one.

components.meaning: horn (from a bird's beak-like tuft, 觜)

compositionNote: 嘴 adds a mouth (口) to the older word 觜 (a bird's horn-like beak tuft, made of 此 phonetic + 角 horn), giving 'mouth' its modern character.
poem: A mouth (口) that says 'this' (此) and more,
shaped like a bird's horned (角) beak of yore,
open wide to chew and speak —
that's your MOUTH (zuǐ), the word you seek.

compositionNote: A body-shaped frame (尸) holds a cloth (巾) next to a blade-like edge (刂), picturing bristles scraping back and forth — hence 'to brush, to swipe'.
poem: A body's (尸) cloth (巾) cut with a blade (刂),
scrubbing back and forth it's made,
bristles sweep in one quick stroke —
to BRUSH, shuā (刷), like magic woke.

components.meaning: a picture of interlocking teeth or tusks

compositionNote: 牙 is a pictograph of two jagged teeth or tusks meshing together, too basic to break into further parts.
poem: Two jagged shapes (牙) that interlock,
like tiny teeth set in a rock,
biting down with sharp array —
that's a TOOTH, pronounced yá (牙).

meanings.def: throughout, the whole (as in 终身)

components.meaning: winter; also a phonetic hint for zhōng

compositionNote: A skein of silk thread (纟) runs out just as winter (冬) closes the year — both images point to reaching 'the end'.
poem: A silk thread's (纟) end meets winter's (冬) chill,
the year runs out, the seasons still,
at last we reach the final door —
that's FINALLY, zhōng (终), and nothing more.

meanings.def: at, in, on, to, than (formal, as in 关于, 由于)

components.meaning: an ancient character originally depicting a curling breath or sigh

compositionNote: 于 is a simple ancient form later borrowed purely as a grammatical particle, too basic to be split into meaningful parts.
poem: A breath (于) curled up and drifting slow,
an ancient sigh from long ago,
now marks 'at', 'in', or 'than' with ease —
that little word is yú (于), if you please.

components.meaning: to walk, move along a road

compositionNote: Walking (辶) along and crossing paths with a strange creature (禺) captures the idea of 'meeting by chance'; 禺 also lends its sound.
poem: While walking (辶) down a winding street,
a monkey-like (禺) stranger you might meet,
by chance your paths cross, quick and new —
that's to MEET someone, yù (遇), it's true.

meanings.def: like, in the manner of (as in 这般, 百般)

components.meaning: a pole or weapon used to push a boat along

compositionNote: A boat (舟) pushed along by a pole (殳) gave the sense of 'a way of doing something' — one manner or kind among many.
poem: A boat (舟) is poled (殳) from shore to shore,
each kind of trip, one way or more,
'like this' or 'such', they mean the same —
that KIND of way, bān (般) is its name.

components.meaning: to arrive (phonetic and semantic: the place one arrives at)

compositionNote: A roof (宀) covers the place you arrive (至) at and stay — the innermost room of a house.
poem: Beneath the roof (宀) where you arrive (至),
a quiet space to rest, alive,
four walls that hold your work or bed —
that's a ROOM, shì (室), safe instead.

compositionNote: A person (亻) settles under a cover (亠) as the moon (夕) rises — the picture of night falling.
poem: Under a roof (亠), a person (亻) lies,
as the pale moon (夕) climbs the skies,
the world grows dark, the stars ignite —
that quiet time is yè (夜), the NIGHT.

meanings.def: to be like, to be as if

compositionNote: A woman's (女) spoken word (口) was once obeyed and followed exactly — giving 如 its sense of 'being like, in accordance with'.
poem: A woman's (女) mouth (口) says what is true,
and others act just as she'd do,
'as if', 'like this' — the meaning's plain —
that's LIKE, pronounced rú (如), again.

meanings.def: this, the current (as in 本人, 本来)

components.meaning: a mark showing the base of the tree

compositionNote: A single line (一) drawn across the base of a tree (木) points to its roots — the 'origin' or 'foundation' of the thing.
poem: A tree (木) marked low with a single line (一),
right at the root, the base, the sign,
where all things start, the very ground —
that's the ROOT, běn (本), origin found.

compositionNote: Ladders were made of wood (木); the little brother (弟) here mainly lends its sound to give tī.
poem: Made of wood (木), your brother (弟) climbs,
step by step, one rung at a time,
up and up to reach the sky —
that's a LADDER, tī (梯), so high.

compositionNote: A small flame (火) fixed on a peg-like stand (丁, also lending its sound) pictures a lamp.
poem: A tiny flame (火) on a nail-like (丁) stand,
glowing warm within your hand,
chasing shadows, giving sight —
that's a LAMP, dēng (灯), bringing light.

meanings.def: adverbial suffix '-ly', pronounced de (as in 慢慢地)

compositionNote: Soil (土) paired with the sound-bearing 也 gives 地, the solid ground beneath everything.
poem: The soil (土) below, and 'also' (也) too,
combine to form the ground for you,
where feet stand firm and roots take hold —
that's the EARTH, called dì (地), so old.

meanings.def: hard, unyielding (figurative, as in 铁的事实)

compositionNote: Metal (钅) combines with the sound-bearing 失 to name 铁, iron — a metal too tough to lose its shape.
poem: A metal (钅) core that's hard to lose (失),
strong and firm, the sort you'd choose,
tracks and tools of gray-black gleam —
that's IRON, tiě (铁), a sturdy dream.

meanings.def: to do, make, handle, play with (as in 弄坏, 弄清楚)
alley, lane (read lòng, as in 弄堂)

components.meaning: jade (form of 玉 used as a component)

compositionNote: Two hands (廾) turning over a piece of jade (王, from 玉) pictured 'playing with' or 'handling' something.
poem: Two hands (廾) hold jade (王) up to the light,
turning, twisting, left then right,
to fiddle, fix, or make it new —
that's TO HANDLE, nòng (弄), what you do.

meanings.def: according to, based on (as in 按照)

compositionNote: A hand (扌) pressing down brings things to rest in peace (安) — the image behind 'to press' and 'to follow (a rule)'.
poem: A hand (扌) brings peace (安) with gentle force,
pressing down along its course,
push the button, calm and true —
that's to PRESS, àn (按), it's up to you.
